a30.speaker: Helen Khungwa Chira, USAID Zambia Nutrition Advisor
a30.name: Helen Khungwa Chira
a30.title: USAID Zambia Nutrition Advisor
a30.speech: Says the Bicycle Innovation Programme (BIP) aims to tackle development challenges in sub-Saharan Africa through the increased adoption of bicycles. "The BIP aims to achieve this by incentivising the development and scaling of innovative solutions relating to bicycles within an open innovation programme structure," she said. ; Said USAID's country development cooperation strategy in Malawi and Zambia has a specific focus on reducing rural poverty through enterprise-driven economic growth.

a188.speaker: Experts in political and economic affairs
a188.name: Experts in political and economic affairs
a188.speech: Advise African countries to prepare for a difficult period of self-reliance and to choose agendas that match these policy changes, while citing several issues, including immigrants and the emphasis on abortion, as the things that brought down his Democratic opponent, Kamala Harris.

a188.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a188.name: Donald Trump
a188.title: US President
a188.speech: Once called African countries, Haiti and El Salvador "shithole countries", complaining that many immigrants come from those countries into his country ; when he came to power in 2016 he called Africans lazy and foolish, saying all they know is eating, having sex and crime.

a188.speaker: African Union
a188.name: African Union
a188.speech: Has already asked the United States Congress to extend AGOA by at least 10 years to continue the programme, a request which may hit a wall.

a188.speaker: Ibrahim Rabby, international affairs analyst
a188.name: Ibrahim Rabby
a188.title: international affairs analyst
a188.speech: Said Trump's victory has many interpretations for Africa, the big question being whether he will be the same as in his first term of 2016 to 2020 or whether he will be new: "Africa needs to understand that Trump's policies cannot change because from the time of his campaign process he did not show that he would change anything, especially when it comes to foreign affairs; he looks more to America and his slogan America Great Again" ; said that if America cannot get anything from Africa, then it cannot pursue any country; instead what he will do is open up the nation on the basis of relations and greater profit ; "For example, in the Middle East he will continue with countries that give America profit, including Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, and he will cut relations with countries that want to depend on that nation" ; "Trump is avoiding what America has been doing for many years for Africa. There is something to learn: from 2016 to 2020 we witnessed African countries carrying out many coups because America, which was seen as the world's prefect, avoided its responsibilities and stopped looking at Africa" ; "Trump's foreign policies are clear and you don't need to go to a classroom to learn to know what he is thinking; changes will occur especially in institutions. In his past term many institutions were closed for lack of funding."

a188.speaker: Ibrahim Rabby, international affairs analyst
a188.name: Ibrahim Rabby
a188.title: international affairs analyst
a188.speech: Said President Joe Biden has not visited Africa more than Kamala Harris, and that with Trump's victory Africa must decide to be self-reliant because such a life is more important.

a188.speaker: Innocent Shoo, lecturer at the Salim Ahmed Salim Diplomacy College
a188.name: Innocent Shoo
a188.title: lecturer at the Salim Ahmed Salim Diplomacy College
a188.speech: Says African countries need to tighten their belts because Trump will control illegal immigration and the giving of aid: "African leaders need to come up with an agenda to control the young people sneaking off to Europe and America to seek a better life. Trump is fed up; he has said that when he takes office he is going to expel all illegal immigrants" ; said Trump's outlook is to heal America and he wants to restore that nation's capability, explaining that Africa ought to organise itself since he has already sounded the alarm ; "We expect the wars in Gaza and Israel, and on the Middle East side, perhaps will end, including also Sudan. He will try to end those wars by talking with the leaders of those countries, so it will help the price of oil to fall."

a188.speaker: Dr Ambassador Morwa, lecturer at Mbeya Catholic University College (CUCoM)
a188.name: Dr Ambassador Morwa
a188.title: lecturer at Mbeya Catholic University College (CUCoM)
a188.speech: Said Trump was elected with the aim of ending the wars going on in various parts of the world: "Many American citizens have been complaining that their tax money is being used to run the war in Ukraine and Russia. With those wars ended, Africa will benefit from oil resources falling in price" ; said those wars have raised the price of oil because they use that energy on a large scale, so with their end a great blessing will emerge and European nations will begin to look at Africa.

a204.speaker: Tshifhiwa Matodzi, former VBS Mutual Bank chairperson (court testimony)
a204.name: Tshifhiwa Matodzi
a204.title: former VBS Mutual Bank chairperson (court testimony)
a204.speech: Who pleaded guilty in the VBS Mutual Bank looting scandal, testified against former Thulamela mayor Avhashoni Stephen Tshifhango, alleging Tshifhango received a Jeep Grand Cherokee as a bribe for facilitating a R30-million deposit from the municipality into VBS ; Implicated other individuals in his testimony, including ANC bigwig Danny Msiza, claiming Msiza pressured Tshifhango to invest and that they, along with former ANC Youth League leader Kabelo Matsepe, met to discuss further investments ; Also alleged that former VBS officials Phophi Mukhodobwane and Solly Maposa managed a slush fund account used to purchase the vehicle for Tshifhango and pay bribes, with evidence presented showing emails about the vehicle financing.

a204.speaker: USAID
a204.name: USAID
a204.speech: Has permanently ended grants for Pepfar-funded HIV organisations in South Africa, citing misaligned priorities and national interest.

a204.speaker: Uber South Africa
a204.name: Uber South Africa
a204.speech: Has expressed sympathy for Sarah Scott and launched an internal investigation, stating their commitment to cooperating with authorities and ensuring the safety of all app users.

a204.speaker: South African Police
a204.name: South African Police
a204.speech: Are currently investigating the incident as an attempted kidnapping.

a204.speaker: Barbara Creecy, Transport Minister (South Africa)
a204.name: Barbara Creecy
a204.title: Transport Minister (South Africa)
a204.speech: Announced the Cabinet’s decision to appoint John Lamola as the new CEO of South African Airways, which follows interviews conducted by herself and Deputy President Paul Mashatile.

a204.speaker: Adan Mendoza, Santa Fe County Sheriff
a204.name: Adan Mendoza
a204.title: Santa Fe County Sheriff
a204.speech: Confirmed the deaths of actor Gene Hackman and his wife Betsy Arakawa, stating there was no immediate indication of foul play.

a226.speaker: Prof. Peter Katjavivi, Speaker of the National Assembly of Namibia
a226.name: Prof. Peter Katjavivi
a226.title: Speaker of the National Assembly of Namibia
a226.speech: Wished fellow MPs the best of wishes for Christmas and a prosperous New Year.

a226.speaker: Loide Kasingo, Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly of Namibia
a226.name: Loide Kasingo
a226.title: Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly of Namibia
a226.speech: Wished fellow MPs the best of wishes for Christmas and a prosperous New Year.

a226.speaker: Agnes Tjongarero, Namibian Minister of Youth, Sport and National Service
a226.name: Agnes Tjongarero
a226.title: Namibian Minister of Youth, Sport and National Service
a226.speech: Wished fellow MPs the best of wishes for Christmas and a prosperous New Year.

a226.name: Hamunyera Hambyuka
a226.title: Swapo Party Chief Whip in the National Assembly
a226.speech: Wished fellow MPs the best of wishes for Christmas and a prosperous New Year.

a227.speaker: Sammy Ogunjimi, Group Managing Director/CEO, Codix Group
a227.name: Sammy Ogunjimi
a227.title: Group Managing Director/CEO, Codix Group
a227.speech: Reacting after receiving the approval, said: "This approval is more than just an achievement for the company, it is a leap forward for Nigeria's healthcare ecosystem, enhancing access to high-quality In-Vitro Diagnostics (IVDs) and driving local production." ; "This is not just a big win for Nigeria, but for the entire African continent, as it is the first time a WHO PQ HIV Test Kit would either be manufactured, assembled or packaged in Africa, and available for procurement by the development partners."

a227.speaker: Sammy Ogunjimi, Group Managing Director/CEO, Codix Group
a227.name: Sammy Ogunjimi
a227.title: Group Managing Director/CEO, Codix Group
a227.speech: Said the company will continue to work in collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Health, NAFDAC and PVAC to make Nigeria a hub for quality diagnostic products in Africa.

a227.speaker: Mary Ogangwu, Chief Operating Officer of Codix Pharma
a227.name: Mary Ogangwu
a227.title: Chief Operating Officer of Codix Pharma
a227.speech: Said "the achievement is the result of tremendous effort, not just from the organisation, but also from international partners and local stakeholders." ; lauded NAFDAC, PVAC, FMOH, and others, for providing invaluable technical support and encouragement to make this a reality. "I also want to highlight the exceptional dedication and sacrifice of our team, led by the GMD, Mr. Sammy Ogunjimi. Their hard work and commitment have been the backbone of our success, and we stand strong, driven by their unwavering support and determination".

a227.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO) (Change Notification approval)
a227.name: World Health Organization (WHO) (Change Notification approval)
a227.speech: Following the successful Change Notification (CN) approval from the WHO, Colexa Biosensor Limited, a subsidiary of Codix Group, is now licensed to package a WHO Prequalified Rapid Diagnostic Test kit at its factory in Nigeria.

a699.speaker: Statement accompanying the AWIEF Growth Accelerator programme application
a699.name: Statement accompanying the AWIEF Growth Accelerator programme application
a699.speech: "This will be achieved by making the WSMEs credit and investment-ready and eligible to access business loans and financing from FSDH Merchant Bank Limited. The programme will provide a stream of businesses that are adequately prepared to meet the FSDH Merchant Bank's credit requirements."

a699.speaker: The organisers (AWIEF, African Guarantee Fund and FSDH Merchant Bank)
a699.name: The organisers (AWIEF
a699.title: African Guarantee Fund and FSDH Merchant Bank)
a699.speech: Said the programme will attract and select a cohort of 100 beneficiaries, comprising women entrepreneurs and founders with businesses registered and operating in Nigeria who will participate in the 12-month Growth Accelerator and will benefit from a wide range of tailored and refined business development mentorship, training, and advisory services; businesses must meet one of the criteria including entrepreneurship and ownership, leadership, products and services, and "Additionally, businesses must be based and operating in Nigeria".

a767.speaker: Representatives of six countries at the Doha talks (joint statement)
a767.name: Representatives of six countries at the Doha talks (joint statement)
a767.speech: “The representatives welcomed the joint declaration between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the AFC/M23, facilitated by the State of Qatar, on their commitments to the ceasefire,” the group said in a joint statement released Tuesday. “An urgent priority to facilitate humanitarian assistance.” ; “We reaffirm our joint position on the urgent need for the disputing parties to resolve this conflict without delay,” the statement said, adding that any solution must align with African Union and United Nations resolutions and uphold the sovereignty and territorial integrity of both countries ; the delegates also addressed the deepening humanitarian crisis in the region, calling for “an urgent and coordinated response” ; “We commend the progress achieved following the joint EAC-SADC summit,” the representatives said, while also recognizing the “significant advancements” symbolized by the signing of the Declaration of Principles in Washington, D.C., on April 25 ; the group expressed full support for ongoing regional mediation led by Togolese President Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé, whose role, they noted, remains “central to building mutual trust, sustaining a ceasefire, and promoting a peaceful resolution.”

a767.speaker: Mediators (unnamed)
a767.name: Mediators (unnamed)
a767.speech: Mediators say the latest agreement marks a step forward.

a767.speaker: International agencies (unnamed)
a767.name: International agencies (unnamed)
a767.speech: Warning of worsening conditions for civilians in eastern DRC.

a851.speaker: Certain members of the National Transition Council (CNT)
a851.name: Certain members of the National Transition Council (CNT)
a851.speech: Put forward arguments to justify the absence of certain articles in the draft constitution.

a851.speaker: Aboubacar Demba Dansoko, member of the national political bureau of the RPG Arc-en-ciel
a851.name: Aboubacar Demba Dansoko
a851.title: member of the national political bureau of the RPG Arc-en-ciel
a851.speech: Reacted strongly to the CNT's arguments: "Everything that is being done is aimed at making people believe that by leaving a vacuum around articles 46, 55 and 65, it has not been said whether the transition authorities will stand in an election... If the safeguards are not put in place, it means that it has not been ruled out that the parties concerned could stand. Yet it is crucial that the transitional provisions explicitly take these articles into account, in order to guarantee that the current authorities cannot stand in any eventual elections. This requirement is not negotiable. For it is inconceivable that the same person should be both referee and player in the electoral process. The RPG therefore calls for a serious and rigorous revision of the draft constitution before any public commitment by the members of the CNT. The country cannot afford an extension beyond 31 December 2024. The transition will not go beyond 31 December 2024, not even by an hour... Guinea, up until 5 September 2021, was an example of independence in the French-speaking world, and it is vital to preserve that heritage by avoiding a return to a chaotic political situation. The time is no longer for circumstantial politics, but for collective responsibility to safeguard the country's future. The RPG Arc-en-Ciel calls once again for the end of the state of exception and for respect of the commitments made to the Guinean people, while remaining vigilant in the face of what it considers to be a headlong rush on the part of the CNT."

a1137.speaker: Damtien Larbli Tchintchibidja, Vice-President of the ECOWAS Commission
a1137.name: Damtien Larbli Tchintchibidja
a1137.title: Vice-President of the ECOWAS Commission
a1137.speech: Said in her opening of the inaugural workshop of the Joint Analysis and Response Planning Working Group (JARP-WG) that the ECOWAS region is facing increasingly complex human security challenges, such as violent extremism, conflict, terrorism, transnational organised crime, climate change, epidemics, poverty, inequality and unconstitutional changes of government.

a1137.speaker: Dr Onyinye Onwuka, ECOWAS Commission's Acting Director of Early Warning
a1137.name: Dr Onyinye Onwuka
a1137.title: ECOWAS Commission's Acting Director of Early Warning
a1137.speech: Noted that these challenges are major threats to regional peace and stability. 'Addressing these human security challenges has never been more urgent, which is why the establishment of the JARP-WG is so crucial.'

a1137.speaker: Dr Onyinye Onwuka, ECOWAS Commission's Acting Director of Early Warning
a1137.name: Dr Onyinye Onwuka
a1137.title: ECOWAS Commission's Acting Director of Early Warning
a1137.speech: Also stressed the need for participants to examine the risks, threats and root causes of instability in the region, and to reflect on how best to anticipate and resolve these issues through a more holistic approach. The JARP-WG tools have been designed to facilitate this kind of in-depth collaborative analysis, and it is up to us to make full use of them, she suggested.

a1137.speaker: Report distributed by the APO Group on behalf of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS)
a1137.name: Report distributed by the APO Group on behalf of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS)
a1137.speech: Stated that the JARP Working Group will address issues related to the five thematic areas of human security of ECOWAS Early Warning, namely security, crime, health, environment and governance. It added that after the opening ceremony of the workshop, the participants attended a series of presentations on various issues relating to early warning in the ECOWAS region, presented by Ms Nanténé Coulibaly, Marcel Bossou and Tunji Olonode, staff members of the Early Warning Department of the ECOWAS Commission.

a1204.speaker: Israel and Hamas (the two sides)
a1204.name: Israel and Hamas (the two sides)
a1204.speech: The ceasefire, mediated by Egypt, Qatar and the United States, has so far stayed on the right track despite several incidents that caused each of the two sides to accuse the other of breaching the agreement.

a1242.speaker: MonitNG, civic technology platform (open letter to Governor Nasir Idris of Kebbi State)
a1242.name: MonitNG
a1242.title: civic technology platform (open letter to Governor Nasir Idris of Kebbi State)
a1242.speech: Has raised the alarm over the deplorable conditions of the Primary Healthcare Centre in Golonga, Sakace Ward, Shanga Local Government Area of Kebbi State, describing the situation as a threat to human dignity and rural survival, noting that it is “devoid of beds, clean water, or electricity” and has a roof “on the verge of collapse” ; “Patients are left to lie on bare mats in a facility devoid of beds, clean water, or electricity. The severely damaged roof is on the verge of collapse, creating a constant sense of fear, especially for mothers and their children seeking care.” ; “This goes beyond neglect; it reflects a profound failure to uphold the basic right to healthcare for rural communities.” ; “Under former Governor Atiku Bagudu, 134 primary health centres were renovated, yet Golonga was inexplicably excluded. Now, preventable diseases like cholera (875 cases in Kebbi in 2024 alone) and maternal deaths continue to rise because facilities like this lack even the most basic equipment for antenatal care and emergency treatment. How many more lives must be lost before the government takes action?”

a1242.speaker: MonitNG, civic technology platform (open letter to Governor Nasir Idris of Kebbi State)
a1242.name: MonitNG
a1242.title: civic technology platform (open letter to Governor Nasir Idris of Kebbi State)
a1242.speech: “Even with billions allocated to healthcare and funding from major donors such as USAID and the Gates Foundation, Golonga Health Post lies deserted, overshadowed by the focus on urban centres.” ; “How have these funds failed to make an impact? Why should expectant mothers endure life-threatening conditions in a facility lacking even the most essential prenatal care tools?”

a1242.speaker: MonitNG, civic technology platform
a1242.name: MonitNG
a1242.title: civic technology platform
a1242.speech: Demanded immediate intervention from the state government, stating: “We demand immediate action from Governor Nasir Idris and the Kebbi State Government. Golonga Health Post needs complete renovation, proper beds, solar power, clean water, medical equipment, and trained staff.” ; “Healthcare is a basic right, not a privilege, for city dwellers. How many more lives must be lost before our leaders fulfil their promises to rural communities?”

a1242.speaker: MonITNG (@monitng), post on X/Twitter, April 17, 2025
a1242.name: MonITNG (@monitng)
a1242.title: post on X/Twitter, April 17, 2025
a1242.speech: “SHOCKING!!! Dear Gov @NasiridrisKG During our visit to the Primary Health Post in Golonga, Sakace Ward, Shanga LGA, Kebbi State, we encountered a deeply distressing reality. Patients are left to lie on bare mats in a facility devoid of beds, clean water, or electricity. The…”

a1416.speaker: Jose Luis Livramento de Brito, Ambassador of Cabo Verde to the United States
a1416.name: Jose Luis Livramento de Brito
a1416.title: Ambassador of Cabo Verde to the United States
a1416.speech: Clarified this fact when contacted by Inforpress about a list circulating on social media claiming that 314 Cape Verdeans are to be sent to the country in the coming days. According to the diplomat, there is no immediate deportation list; however, many Cape Verdeans already have a judge's order and have only not been deported because they have not yet been detained by the American police. As he explained, the number has been accumulating over the years and what can be confirmed is that they will only be deported if they are caught committing some crime.

a1416.speaker: Jose Filomeno Monteiro, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Cabo Verde
a1416.name: Jose Filomeno Monteiro
a1416.title: Minister of Foreign Affairs of Cabo Verde
a1416.speech: Said on Friday the 24th that the Government is working on a contingency plan to support the Cape Verdean community in the United States with regard to a possible deportation of illegal immigrants. As he stated, a large proportion of Cape Verdean citizens residing in the USA have legalised status, stressing that the Government views the choices made by the United States with "naturalness", respecting the country's sovereignty.

a1416.speaker: Ulisses Correia e Silva, Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a1416.name: Ulisses Correia e Silva
a1416.title: Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a1416.speech: Acknowledged in an interview with RCV that the measures announced by the new administration regarding illegal deportation raise some concern on the part of the authorities, but assured that the country is prepared to receive the possible repatriates.

a1416.speaker: United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement
a1416.name: United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement
a1416.speech: According to the United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement service, on Thursday the 23rd a total of 538 foreigners were arrested and 373 were placed in detention in the first actions following Trump's decree.

a1416.speaker: United States Department of Homeland Security (data)
a1416.name: United States Department of Homeland Security (data)
a1416.speech: According to data from the United States Department of Homeland Security, the goal of one million deportations a year set by the Republican is considered double the maximum number of deportations carried out in a single year in recent decades.

a1525.speaker: 2024 Nigeria Demographic and Health Survey (NDHS) report
a1525.name: 2024 Nigeria Demographic and Health Survey (NDHS) report
a1525.speech: Has revealed that only three in 10 married Nigerian women can make informed decisions about their sexual and reproductive health; just 29 per cent of currently married women aged 15 to 49 report having a say on all three key aspects of reproductive health: sexual relations, contraceptive use, and their own healthcare ; highlights education and household wealth as major determinants of women's decision-making power, showing that only nine per cent of women with no formal education can make informed choices on all three indicators, compared with 58 per cent of those with more than secondary education, and that just nine per cent of women in the lowest wealth quintile report full reproductive health autonomy compared with 58 per cent among the wealthiest households ; suggests that poverty and lack of education remain the most significant barriers to women's empowerment in reproductive health, regardless of age or location ; shows that the contraceptive prevalence rate stands at 20 per cent among married women and 50 per cent among sexually active unmarried women, and reveals an unmet need for family planning among 21 per cent of married women and 36 per cent of sexually active unmarried women, highlighting the persistent weaknesses in service delivery.

a1525.speaker: Lewis Aituma, family planning advocate and Fellow of the West African College of Surgeons, Faculty of Obstetrics and Gynaecology
a1525.name: Lewis Aituma
a1525.title: family planning advocate and Fellow of the West African College of Surgeons, Faculty of Obstetrics and Gynaecology
a1525.speech: Said the NDHS finding reflects "a gross inadequacy in the uptake of reproductive health services among women." He also identified sociocultural beliefs, myths about contraceptive safety, and women's limited autonomy as key barriers to progress ; "In many African settings, women still depend on their husbands' approval to use family planning, which undermines their right to make independent reproductive choices."

a1525.speaker: Lewis Aituma, family planning advocate and Fellow of the West African College of Surgeons, Faculty of Obstetrics and Gynaecology
a1525.name: Lewis Aituma
a1525.title: family planning advocate and Fellow of the West African College of Surgeons, Faculty of Obstetrics and Gynaecology
a1525.speech: Added that empowering women, improving awareness, and ensuring access to affordable contraceptive services are vital to reducing maternal deaths and improving public health outcomes ; "A way to enhance the uptake of this vital reproductive health service will be to enhance awareness among women, empower women, create access to contraceptive services at affordable prices, enact laws that seek to control population explosion, enhance the rights of women to seek reproductive health services of their choice, training and retraining of health personnel to offer adequate and comprehensive reproductive health services to women at clinical contacts."

a1525.speaker: PREMIUM TIMES analysis of the 2025 budget
a1525.name: PREMIUM TIMES analysis of the 2025 budget
a1525.speech: Shows that the federal government slashed family planning funding by 97 per cent, allocating N66.39 million compared to N2.2 billion in 2024.

a1525.speaker: Experts (unnamed)
a1525.name: Experts (unnamed)
a1525.speech: Have warned that these reductions could reverse progress made in reproductive health, leading to more unintended pregnancies, higher maternal deaths, and even the collapse of family planning programmes if not addressed.

a1688.speaker: Romuald Wadagni, Minister of Economy and Finance of Benin
a1688.name: Romuald Wadagni
a1688.title: Minister of Economy and Finance of Benin
a1688.speech: In a reply to a letter sent by the Managing Director of Benin Control, Minister Wadagni reveals the tax exemptions in question. They consist, he says, of exemptions from customs duties and taxes, and from taxes.

a1688.speaker: Government of Benin
a1688.name: Government of Benin
a1688.speech: Invoked the procurement contract that legalises the exemption granted to Benin Control, brandishing the contract that the company signed with the State - a contract nevertheless already terminated under President Boni Yayi.

a1811.speaker: Michelle Bachelet, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
a1811.name: Michelle Bachelet
a1811.title: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
a1811.speech: "While we welcome the Ethiopian Government's statement that there would be unimpeded humanitarian access, in line with the agreement with the UN signed on 29 November, this needs to be to all areas of Tigray where civilians have been affected by the fighting." ; "If civilians were deliberately killed by a party or parties to the conflict, these killings would amount to war crimes and there needs to be, as I have stressed previously, independent, impartial, thorough and transparent investigations to establish accountability and ensure justice." ; "It is essential that there are investigations into allegations of human rights violations there against both Amharans and Tigrayans" ; "What has happened in Tigray over these past seven weeks is as heart-breaking as it is appalling. Despite the Ethiopian Government's initial efforts to provide humanitarian aid in some areas, it is vital that life-saving assistance is delivered to all civilian populations in need [in Tigray] without further delay"

a1811.speaker: UN human rights (UNHCR) report
a1811.name: UN human rights (UNHCR) report
a1811.speech: "We have received allegations concerning violations of international humanitarian law and human rights law, including artillery strikes on populated areas, the deliberate targeting of civilians, extrajudicial killings and widespread looting." ; Stated that one of "the most shocking incidents reported to date was the alleged mass killing of several hundred people, mainly Amharans, in Mai Kadra, on 9 November." ; "Based on multiple accounts, the Amhara 'Fano' militia has reportedly committed human rights abuses, including killing civilians and carrying out looting." ; "For instance, while the Government of Ethiopia has repeatedly alleged that the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) forces have been involved in violations of international law, without access it remains challenging to verify these allegations." ; Cited "that fighting is said to be continuing, particularly in some areas of north, central and southern Tigray" and complained of "the continuing lack of overall humanitarian access, coupled with an ongoing communications blackout in many areas"

a1811.speaker: Witnesses cited in the UN report (anonymous)
a1811.name: Witnesses cited in the UN report (anonymous)
a1811.speech: Charged "The Ethiopian army and regional Amhara forces and militia" for "allegedly killing civilians and looting the hospital, banks, businesses, supermarkets and private houses."

a1811.speaker: Amnesty International and the Ethiopian Human Rights Commission
a1811.name: Amnesty International and the Ethiopian Human Rights Commission
a1811.speech: Have recognised the Mai Kadra mass killing as genocidal.

a1811.speaker: Government of Ethiopia
a1811.name: Government of Ethiopia
a1811.speech: Has repeatedly alleged that Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) forces have been involved in violations of international law.

a1811.speaker: Mike Pompeo, US Secretary of State
a1811.name: Mike Pompeo
a1811.title: US Secretary of State
a1811.speech: Promptly and unequivocally denounced the threats and firing of rockets on civilian targets in the cities of Gondar and Bahir Dar.

a1811.speaker: TPLF (cabal)
a1811.name: TPLF (cabal)
a1811.speech: Pompously admitted the threats and firing of rockets on civilian targets in the cities of Gondar and Bahir Dar.

a1838.speaker: International news outlets such as Reuters, The New York Times and CNN
a1838.name: International news outlets such as Reuters
a1838.title: The New York Times and CNN
a1838.speech: Reported yesterday that the MCC, a US Government agency funding development projects in poorer nations, may close due to budget cuts.

a1838.speaker: Reuters (citing a staff meeting and an e-mail communication)
a1838.name: Reuters (citing a staff meeting and an e-mail communication)
a1838.speech: Reported that MCC staff were told in a meeting on Wednesday that all of the agency's programmes would be closed and that staff numbers would be minimised; further reported that Kim told the staff that officials from the Department of Government Efficiency headed by multi-billionaire Elon Musk visited MCC early last week and entered in talks with the leadership, who were attempting to save the agency.

a1838.speaker: Kyeh Kim, Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) senior official
a1838.name: Kyeh Kim
a1838.title: Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) senior official
a1838.speech: "Foreign aid is not a priority for the administration and so MCC's work needs to wind down," as quoted by Reuters as having told staff.

a1838.speaker: Marcus Muhariwa, US Embassy strategic communications specialist (non-response)
a1838.name: Marcus Muhariwa
a1838.title: US Embassy strategic communications specialist (non-response)
a1838.speech: When asked if MCC-funded projects in Malawi would face immediate termination if the shutdown proceeds, said he would respond when the response is ready; however, he had not replied by the time the paper went to press at 9pm.

a1838.speaker: Williams Banda, Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs spokesperson (non-response)
a1838.name: Williams Banda
a1838.title: Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs spokesperson (non-response)
a1838.speech: Said in a brief WhatsApp response that he needed more time to review the matter.

a1838.speaker: Madalitso Mbendera, Millennium Challenge Account (MCA) Malawi II communications director
a1838.name: Madalitso Mbendera
a1838.title: Millennium Challenge Account (MCA) Malawi II communications director
a1838.speech: Said the office was still waiting for the official direction from MCC on what the development means for Malawi: "Once we have more clarity, we will share updates. For now, our 2024 Annual Recap on the official website shows progress since May 6."

a1838.speaker: MCA Malawi II 2024 Annual Recap (report on official website)
a1838.name: MCA Malawi II 2024 Annual Recap (report on official website)
a1838.speech: Shows that MCA Malawi II began road construction under the Accelerated Growth Corridors Project in September 2024.

a1838.speaker: Dye Mawindo, MCA-Malawi II chief executive officer
a1838.name: Dye Mawindo
a1838.title: MCA-Malawi II chief executive officer
a1838.speech: In an earlier interview, said he was confident that they will complete the construction of four roads at a combined length of 280km in three years, which will be way ahead of the five-year compact period.

a1838.speaker: Mannes Nkhata, Farmers Union of Malawi president
a1838.name: Mannes Nkhata
a1838.title: Farmers Union of Malawi president
a1838.speech: Reacting to news of the potential shutdown of MCC, said it would be a blow to the country's agriculture sector and development of transport infrastructure in general: "If the project really gets terminated, ultimate losers will be rural poor farmers, including women and those living with various disabilities who had all their hopes on this project as a gateway to access reliable input markets and profitable output markets."

a2079.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State and acting administrator of USAID
a2079.name: Marco Rubio
a2079.title: US Secretary of State and acting administrator of USAID
a2079.speech: States that the Agency has long strayed from its original mission of responsibly promoting American interests abroad, and "it is now abundantly clear that significant portions of USAID funding are not aligned with the core national interests of the United States."

a2079.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State and acting administrator of USAID
a2079.name: Marco Rubio
a2079.title: US Secretary of State and acting administrator of USAID
a2079.speech: Informed Congress that a review of USAID's foreign assistance activities is under way with a view to a possible reorganisation.

a2079.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State and acting administrator of USAID
a2079.name: Marco Rubio
a2079.title: US Secretary of State and acting administrator of USAID
a2079.speech: "As we evaluate USAID and ensure it is aligned with an America First agenda and the efforts of the State Department, we will continue to protect the interests of the American people and ensure that their tax money is not wasted."

a2119.speaker: Prof. Peter Abraham, Chancellor and Vice Chancellor (Africa), Heart Bible International University and Seminary (letter dated 10 July 2024)
a2119.name: Prof. Peter Abraham
a2119.title: Chancellor and Vice Chancellor (Africa), Heart Bible International University and Seminary (letter dated 10 July 2024)
a2119.speech: "On behalf of Heart Bible International University and Seminary, an institution dedicated to enriching great minds, I am delighted to extend my heartfelt congratulations on your well-deserved nomination. Your dedication, hard work, and outstanding contributions have not gone unnoticed. It is an honour to see your name put forward for this nomination for honorary Professor in Humanitarianism" ; "Considering all your contributions and humanitarian services to the community and Africa at large, your belief in the transformative power of education and your mission in empowering the next generation with your numerous scholarships, the University would be pleased to honour you with the award of Presidential Lifetime Achievement Award and honorary Professor in Humanitarianism."

a2119.speaker: Heart Bible International University and Seminary (institution)
a2119.name: Heart Bible International University and Seminary (institution)
a2119.speech: Emphasized that it takes pride in being authorized to acknowledge outstanding leaders for their contributions to community service and humanitarian efforts, and the letter further affirmed that Bishop Adegbite is being honoured for his excellent work over the years and his commitment to development.

a2253.speaker: Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights (statement to AFP)
a2253.name: Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights (statement to AFP)
a2253.speech: "As of 21 July, we recorded 1,054 people killed in Gaza while trying to obtain food; 766 of them were killed near Gaza Humanitarian Foundation (GHF) sites and 288 near aid convoys of the UN and of other humanitarian organisations," alleging that these people were killed "by the Israeli army" ; "Our data is based on information from various reliable sources on the ground, including medical teams and humanitarian and human rights organisations."

a2253.speaker: The UN and the main aid organisations
a2253.name: The UN and the main aid organisations
a2253.speech: Have refused to work with the GHF, arguing that the foundation serves Israeli military objectives and violates basic humanitarian principles.

a2253.speaker: European Union diplomacy
a2253.name: European Union diplomacy
a2253.speech: Said today that killing civilians seeking aid in Gaza is "indefensible".

a2253.speaker: Kaja Kallas, EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy
a2253.name: Kaja Kallas
a2253.title: EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy
a2253.speech: "I made it very clear that the Israeli army must stop killing people at the distribution points" of humanitarian aid, she said on social media after a meeting with the Israeli Foreign Minister, Gideon Saar.

a2255.speaker: Gates Foundation (announcement on its website)
a2255.name: Gates Foundation (announcement on its website)
a2255.speech: Announced a $1.6 billion commitment to Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, over the next five years to help deliver lifesaving vaccines to children in the world's most vulnerable communities.

a2255.speaker: Bill Gates, chair of the Gates Foundation
a2255.name: Bill Gates
a2255.title: chair of the Gates Foundation
a2255.speech: Warned that for the first time in decades, the number of kids dying around the world will likely go up this year instead of down because of massive cuts to foreign aid. "That is a tragedy," Mr Gates said, noting that fully funding Gavi is the single most powerful step to take to stop the tragedy. ; "The legacy of our generation cannot be that we looked away as millions of poor children died of preventable causes." ; "The world now has affordable, effective, proven tools that save lives. Wealthy nations should fully fund Gavi and the Global Fund, the organisations created to get those products to the people who need them."

a2255.speaker: Gates Foundation
a2255.name: Gates Foundation
a2255.speech: Said international development programmes have been severely impacted by declining budgets and shifting political priorities ; explained that after years of stagnation, foreign assistance plummeted this year, putting at risk the hard-won progress in child survival and public health made over the last 25 years.

a2255.speaker: Gates Foundation
a2255.name: Gates Foundation
a2255.speech: Noted that early donor pledges to Gavi reflect broad support for immunisation as a high-impact investment, as well as confidence in multilateral collaboration to accelerate progress on global health ; said it has committed more than $30.6 billion to advance vaccines since 2000, of which $7.7 billion has been directed to Gavi, making it the foundation's largest grantee ; said it will work together with its partners to make as much progress as possible towards three primary goals: ending preventable deaths of mothers and babies; preventing deadly infectious diseases in the next generation; lifting millions out of poverty by expanding opportunities.

a2255.speaker: Gates Foundation
a2255.name: Gates Foundation
a2255.speech: "Despite that progress, one in five children still lack access to essential vaccines, and outbreaks of preventable diseases-including measles and meningitis-are increasing, threatening to reverse decades of gains" ; said Gavi's co-financing model emphasises country ownership and long-term sustainability, noting that as partner countries' economies grow, they contribute more to their vaccine programmes and eventually transition to self-financing: "Since 2000, 19 countries have successfully graduated from Gavi support."

a2334.speaker: National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE) (statement released last week)
a2334.name: National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE) (statement released last week)
a2334.speech: Announced that it has granted licenses to five private non-bank entities - Dugda Fidelity Investment Plc, Ethio Independent Foreign Exchange Bureau, Global Independent Foreign Exchange Bureau, Robust Independent Foreign Exchange Bureau, and Yoga Forex Bureau - to operate in the foreign exchange market, stating that these entities will offer services from spot transactions to various commercial forex activities and are permitted to handle up to 10pc of the daily forex auction limit set by the central bank.

a2334.speaker: Market analysts
a2334.name: Market analysts
a2334.speech: Say the introduction of non-bank players could reduce the parallel foreign exchange market, where rates have soared to unprecedented levels due to high demand and scarce supply.

a2334.speaker: World Bank and the International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2334.name: World Bank and the International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2334.speech: Have urged the federal government to implement reforms to beef up currency stability, including liberalising the forex market.

a2341.speaker: Michel Olivier Lacharité, head of emergencies at Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)
a2341.name: Michel Olivier Lacharité
a2341.title: head of emergencies at Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)
a2341.speech: Said in a statement: "People are not just trapped in fierce and blind fighting", stating that people are also targeted by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and their allies "mainly because of their ethnicity."

a2341.speaker: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) report "Besieged, attacked, starved"
a2341.name: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) report "Besieged
a2341.title: attacked, starved"
a2341.speech: Warns of the risk of a "bloodbath" in El-Fasher, where about 800,000 people have been besieged by the paramilitaries since May 2024 ; the report, compiled from 80 testimonies collected between May 2024 and May 2025, describes "systematic patterns of violence, including looting, massacres, sexual violence, abductions, starvation" and attacks on civilian infrastructure.

a2341.speaker: Witnesses cited by MSF
a2341.name: Witnesses cited by MSF
a2341.speech: Said RSF soldiers plan to "cleanse El-Fasher" of its non-Arab communities, in particular the Zaghawa ethnic group, a pillar of the Joint Forces allied with the army, raising fears of a massacre after the atrocities committed in 2023 against the Masalit in western Darfur.

a2341.speaker: Mathilde Simon, humanitarian affairs adviser at MSF
a2341.name: Mathilde Simon
a2341.title: humanitarian affairs adviser at MSF
a2341.speech: "We fear that such a scenario will be repeated in El-Fasher."

a2341.speaker: António Guterres, UN Secretary-General
a2341.name: António Guterres
a2341.title: UN Secretary-General
a2341.speech: Said on Friday that he was trying to negotiate a ceasefire to allow humanitarian aid to be sent to El-Fasher.

a2341.speaker: United Nations
a2341.name: United Nations
a2341.speech: Describes the conflict as "the largest current humanitarian crisis" ; according to the UN, in northern Darfur alone more than a million people are on the brink of famine.

a2351.speaker: Barthelemy Toguo, Cameroonian visual artist
a2351.name: Barthelemy Toguo
a2351.title: Cameroonian visual artist
a2351.speech: Said he travelled to Benin because he wanted to share his career path with young artists of the African continent: "I came here to share this moment, to exchange with them and also to discover what they are doing."

a2351.speaker: Barthelemy Toguo, Cameroonian visual artist
a2351.name: Barthelemy Toguo
a2351.title: Cameroonian visual artist
a2351.speech: Said he is a Cameroonian visual artist who lives and works in Paris and in western Cameroon, in Bandjoun, where he created an artists residency open to artists from around the world working in collaboration with the local community, and that an agricultural dimension was added to the project, with two to three hectares of coffee, banana, maize and oil palm planted using organic methods.

a2351.speaker: Barthelemy Toguo, Cameroonian visual artist
a2351.name: Barthelemy Toguo
a2351.title: Cameroonian visual artist
a2351.speech: Said they developed a critical project on the price of raw materials, deciding to plant, harvest, hull, dry and roast their own coffee and package it with an artist work in order to set the price themselves: "it is up to us Africans, the countries producing such goods, it is up to us to set the price."

a2351.speaker: Leopold Sedar Senghor (quoted by Barthelemy Toguo)
a2351.name: Leopold Sedar Senghor (quoted by Barthelemy Toguo)
a2351.speech: Had said that the prices of raw materials were set by the West, and that it was the West that set the market prices of export products, setting very low prices which impoverished African farmers.

a2351.speaker: Barthelemy Toguo, Cameroonian visual artist
a2351.name: Barthelemy Toguo
a2351.title: Cameroonian visual artist
a2351.speech: Said he began with sculpture at the School of Fine Arts in Abidjan, continued in Grenoble where he discovered photography, Photoshop and performance, and uses painting, sculpture, photography and engraving in his work; said he is lucky to live from what he does because he works with a gallery based in Paris and New York that takes his work to fairs in Basel, Hong Kong, Madrid, Miami and Asia ; Said he entered the school of fine arts around 1990 and finished ten years later, after four years in Abidjan, four in Grenoble and two in Dusseldorf, settling in Paris in 2000.

a2351.speaker: Barthelemy Toguo, Cameroonian visual artist
a2351.name: Barthelemy Toguo
a2351.title: Cameroonian visual artist
a2351.speech: Said he took up agriculture because he thought about the quality of what can be eaten and to escape the daily routine of calls and appointments with exhibition curators, choosing healthy, plant-based agriculture far from toxic, chemical products.

a2351.speaker: Barthelemy Toguo, Cameroonian visual artist
a2351.name: Barthelemy Toguo
a2351.title: Cameroonian visual artist
a2351.speech: Said he left his studio in Paris to build Bandjoun Station alone on family land, without any subsidy, and that the daily difficulty is running it: "we have no subsidy, no budget"; said the difficulties lie in day-to-day funding "because African states do not invest in culture, whereas culture is a concrete factor of development", adding "We stumble, but we move forward with great difficulty."

a2351.speaker: Barthelemy Toguo, Cameroonian visual artist
a2351.name: Barthelemy Toguo
a2351.title: Cameroonian visual artist
a2351.speech: Said he is very attentive to what happens around us and to daily life, drawing on the example of Renaissance artists who painted the plague in Florence: "I am living through a period in which we live with AIDS, Ebola, Covid, and plenty of other things, and I must simply draw inspiration from it."

a2351.speaker: Barthelemy Toguo, Cameroonian visual artist
a2351.name: Barthelemy Toguo
a2351.title: Cameroonian visual artist
a2351.speech: Said that returning to Africa and building Bandjoun Station is a strong symbolic act and that he has carried an idea of solidarity and sharing since his beginnings, adding that he left the Basel fair to come to Benin because the project bearer Christel Gbaguidi had struck him: "That is how Africa must move forward today, by joining hands."

a2351.speaker: Barthelemy Toguo, Cameroonian visual artist
a2351.name: Barthelemy Toguo
a2351.title: Cameroonian visual artist
a2351.speech: Said Beninese contemporary art is quite dynamic and that Christel Gbaguidi and a few rare others are doing concrete things, describing his project as unifying, ambitious and carried alone; said that although he has been present at the Louvre, the Quai Branly museum and the Australia Biennale, African artists are very absent on the continent and it is important to be present and visible there; said "the Beninese State must wake up and take into account this energy that he is introducing into the artistic scene in Benin" and consolidate such a project for the development of the country.

a2351.speaker: Barthelemy Toguo, Cameroonian visual artist
a2351.name: Barthelemy Toguo
a2351.title: Cameroonian visual artist
a2351.speech: Called on all Beninese to show solidarity and to have positive ideas rather than criticism that delays constructive initiatives, said he would return to Benin for other ambitious cultural projects, and said Cameroon is going through a very difficult period because the State has stopped and the situation is blocked.

a2354.speaker: UNAids (feature story)
a2354.name: UNAids (feature story)
a2354.speech: Notes that approximately 85 percent of Malawi HIV and Aids budget depends on donor funding, with the Global Fund supporting antiretroviral procurement through at least 2027.

a2354.speaker: WHO and UNAids
a2354.name: WHO and UNAids
a2354.speech: Have repeatedly urged countries to increase domestic funding amid growing global aid fatigue.

a2354.speaker: Malawi delegation to the International Aids Society Conference in Kigali
a2354.name: Malawi delegation to the International Aids Society Conference in Kigali
a2354.speech: Joined others in calling for sustainable financing mechanisms, such as health taxes, social insurance and increased budgetary allocations, to ensure continuity of HIV services regardless of donor decisions.

a2419.speaker: Office of the Accountant General of the Federation (published data)
a2419.name: Office of the Accountant General of the Federation (published data)
a2419.speech: Data published shows that states received a sum of N128.7 billion as Ecological Funds between December 2023 and February 2025, representing a 15-month period, with month-by-month allocations to states and local governments (for example, in February 2025 N6.036 billion to states and N5.030 billion to local governments).

a2419.speaker: Hussaini Ibrahim, acting Director General, Niger State Emergency Management Agency (NSEMA)
a2419.name: Hussaini Ibrahim
a2419.title: acting Director General, Niger State Emergency Management Agency (NSEMA)
a2419.speech: Told SaharaReporters on Monday that the casualty figure had risen to 153.

a2419.speaker: United Nations Children's Education Fund (UNICEF) statement on its website
a2419.name: United Nations Children's Education Fund (UNICEF) statement on its website
a2419.speech: Noted in 2022 that 2.5 million people in Nigeria were in need of humanitarian assistance due to flooding, sixty percent of these said to be children: "The floods, which have affected 34 out of the 36 states in the country, have displaced 1.3 million people. Over 600 people have lost their lives and over 200,000 houses have either been partially or fully damaged."

a2419.speaker: Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP)
a2419.name: Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP)
a2419.speech: Urged then President Muhammadu Buhari in 2022 to "direct the Attorney General of the Federation and Minister of Justice Mr Abubakar Malami, SAN, and appropriate anti-corruption agencies to promptly and thoroughly investigate the spending of Ecological Fund by governments at all levels - federal, state and local governments from 2001 to 2022."

a2419.speaker: SaharaReporters (earlier report)
a2419.name: SaharaReporters (earlier report)
a2419.speech: Earlier reported that the devastating floods that swept through Mokwa in Niger State in May laid bare the fragility of human security in the face of nature's fury - and the systemic failure of governance structures meant to prevent such calamities; at least 200 lives have been reported to have been lost, with thousands of people displaced.

a2527.speaker: Cllr. Tiawan Saye Gongloe, former presidential candidate and leader of the Liberian People's Party (LPP)
a2527.name: Cllr. Tiawan Saye Gongloe
a2527.title: former presidential candidate and leader of the Liberian People's Party (LPP)
a2527.speech: attributes Liberia's underdevelopment and widespread poverty to shortsighted leadership, decades of mismanagement, and corruption; delivering a keynote address on the topic “A Call for Transformative Change: Liberia's Path to Prosperity,” he noted that Liberia is faced with the undeniable truth that, despite its vast resources, it remains one of the poorest nations in the world ; “This paradox is not the result of a lack of natural wealth; rather, it stems from decades of mismanagement, corruption, and short-sighted leadership. Today, we must ask: What kind of Liberia do we want to build? A nation forever dependent on foreign aid, or a self-sufficient, productive, and thriving Liberia?” ; “Why is this the case? Despite the wealth beneath our soil, many Liberians lack access to basic services like education, healthcare, food security, and infrastructure. Our continued poverty is not a result of resource scarcity, but rather poor governance and the prioritization of personal gain over national development.”

a2527.speaker: Cllr. Tiawan Saye Gongloe, leader of the Liberian People's Party (LPP)
a2527.name: Cllr. Tiawan Saye Gongloe
a2527.title: leader of the Liberian People's Party (LPP)
a2527.speech: argued that when President Boakai took office, he promised a “Rescue Mission” to transform Liberia and his governance experience raised hopes for real progress: “Yet today, poverty still grips our nation, and it is clear that what we need is not just a change in leadership, but a revolution in governance – one that places the needs of the people above the wants of the few”; he continues that Liberia's future requires bold action, systemic reform, and a commitment to responsible, people-centered leadership.

a2527.speaker: Cllr. Tiawan Saye Gongloe, leader of the Liberian People's Party (LPP)
a2527.name: Cllr. Tiawan Saye Gongloe
a2527.title: leader of the Liberian People's Party (LPP)
a2527.speech: Speaking of cutting waste and redirecting resources, he recommends that eliminating waste in government be the first step toward transformation, says it's unacceptable for government officials to continue enjoying lavish salaries, foreign travel, and excessive state functions while most Liberians struggle to access basic services, and urges the government to cut wasteful expenditures and reallocate funds to sectors that will drive real development, such as education, healthcare, infrastructure, and agriculture ; “Look at nations such as Botswana, Rwanda, and Mauritius – countries with fewer resources than Liberia that have managed to build thriving economies through human development, good governance, and wise resource management. If they can do it, so can we. Liberia has the resources and the potential; what we lack is leadership that prioritizes the people's needs over political interests.”

a2527.speaker: Joseph Boakai, President of Liberia
a2527.name: Joseph Boakai
a2527.title: President of Liberia
a2527.speech: when he took office, he promised a “Rescue Mission” to transform Liberia (as reported by Cllr. Gongloe).

a2882.speaker: UNICEF
a2882.name: UNICEF
a2882.speech: The UN agency for the welfare of children has warned that some 110 million children in North Africa and the Middle East live in countries affected by war, with homes, schools and health facilities damaged or destroyed in fighting ; UNICEF estimates indicate that 45 million children across the region will require humanitarian assistance in 2025, a 41 per cent increase since 2020 ; the outlook for 2026 also remains bleak, UNICEF said, noting that its funding for Middle East and North Africa is projected to decline by 20 to 25 per cent, potentially resulting in shortfalls of up to $370 million.

a2882.speaker: Edouard Beigbeder, UNICEF Regional Director for the Middle East and North Africa
a2882.name: Edouard Beigbeder
a2882.title: UNICEF Regional Director for the Middle East and North Africa
a2882.speech: "A child's life is being turned upside down the equivalent of every five seconds due to the conflicts in the region" ; said this would jeopardise lifesaving programmes across the region, including treatment for severe malnutrition, safe water production in conflict zones and vaccinations against deadly diseases ; "As the plight of children in the region worsens, the resources to respond are becoming sparser" ; "Conflicts must stop. International advocacy to resolve these crises must intensify. And support for vulnerable children must increase, not decline."

a2998.speaker: Ben Malunga Phiri, Thyolo Central lawmaker, presenting the DPP's reaction to the budget
a2998.name: Ben Malunga Phiri
a2998.title: Thyolo Central lawmaker, presenting the DPP's reaction to the budget
a2998.speech: Said the 2025-26 budget framework fell short of inspiring hope, adding that it was unrealistic and hard to implement; said at K8.05 trillion the budget was "too exorbitant and too ambitious" because revenue generation, at K5.5 trillion, was low ; "Fellow Malawians, you can see for yourself that this budget is a big lie. The budget has a deficit of K2.47 trillion. Where will the money to fill the deficit come from? Again, borrowing is the only answer. Malawians, you must be worried because MCP is ready to put more debt burden on your shoulders and a yoke of debt around the necks of your children."

a2998.speaker: Ben Malunga Phiri, Thyolo Central lawmaker (DPP)
a2998.name: Ben Malunga Phiri
a2998.title: Thyolo Central lawmaker (DPP)
a2998.speech: "Fellow Malawians, the 2025-26 budget is unrealistic due to its continued overreliance on donor support at a time global dynamics point to heavy deductions in foreign aid. The budget is counting on K1.14 trillion of donor grants. Recently, USaid announced closure. Unfortunately, we are yet to be addressed on how the government intends to manage job loses due to the cut with about 5,000 Malawians affected, [they have not told us] how they intend to fund the services that were previously funded by USaid" ; added that the United Kingdom government, too, had announced that it would reduce budget spending, with international development or foreign aid experiencing cuts ; "Malawians, you must expect more economic trouble. What kind of government is this that has the guts to increase budget expenditures at a time when revenues are falling? Malawians, forget about Malawi 2063. The structure of the 2025-26 budget has little to offer in implementation of the Malawi 2063 vision."

a2998.speaker: Ishmael Nkumba, UDF spokesperson on finance
a2998.name: Ishmael Nkumba
a2998.title: UDF spokesperson on finance
a2998.speech: Said the national budget had wrong assumptions on economic growth rates and added that the UDF was not convinced that economic transformation, characterised by a 3.2 percent growth rate, would be attainable ; "We are concerned about the prolonged imbalance of foreign exchange reserves due to the low capacity to export high value goods and services. While we appreciate the latest measures taken by the Minister of Trade and Industry Vitumbiko Mumba, through the Prohibition Order of 2025, to lower imports of products that can be produced locally, the UDF feels that local producers have neither been capacitated nor incentivised to meet the growing local demand for those foreign goods and services" ; "We, however, implore the government to enhance foreign exchange control measures to safeguard the little forex that we have and to deal with unscrupulous businesses and individuals who are fuelling [activities on] the black market."

a2998.speaker: Simplex Chithyola Banda, Finance Minister of Malawi
a2998.name: Simplex Chithyola Banda
a2998.title: Finance Minister of Malawi
a2998.speech: Hit back at the DPP, accusing the party of "messing up the economy" through over-borrowing, eroding donor confidence and presenting "fictitious reports to International Monetary Fund (IMF)"; said the government was putting up long-lasting financial architecture that would not only help in stabilising the economy but also stimulate economic growth; said the DPP is not an option for Malawi as it allegedly "invented institutionalised corruption and orchestrated anarchy in this country, where people with albinism were killed like chickens" ; "You can't trust such people; people who used to abuse presidential powers."

a2998.speaker: Gladys Ganda, chairperson of the Budget and Finance Committee of Parliament
a2998.name: Gladys Ganda
a2998.title: chairperson of the Budget and Finance Committee of Parliament
a2998.speech: Said the committee was concerned with the significant jump in expenditure at a time revenue was set to rise marginally; said the budget was poised to increase to K8.1 trillion from a 2024-25 revised estimate of K6.1 trillion, representing an increase of K2.0 trillion, while revenue was projected to only grow by K952.21 billion ; "This implies a widening fiscal gap, further exacerbating an already unsustainable debt burden. The committee, therefore, reiterates the urgent need for fiscal discipline, prioritisation of expenditure and enhanced revenue generation to ensure long-term sustainability."

a3067.speaker: Coface (credit insurer, half-yearly country risk assessment)
a3067.name: Coface (credit insurer
a3067.title: half-yearly country risk assessment)
a3067.speech: Maintained Morocco's country risk rating at "B" in its latest half-yearly assessment published in June, a moderate rating confirming the Kingdom's position as the most resilient country in the Maghreb in terms of economic stability and corporate solvency ; according to Coface, this resilience is explained by the relative stability of the Moroccan macroeconomic framework, the gradual diversification of its economy and its capacity to absorb exogenous shocks ; according to Coface, Algeria, plagued by heavy dependence on hydrocarbons, a poorly diversified economy and persistent socio-political tensions, shows a higher risk, while Tunisia's risk profile is heavily penalised and Libya remains classified among the countries at extreme risk.

a3067.speaker: Coface (credit insurer)
a3067.name: Coface (credit insurer)
a3067.speech: Nevertheless highlights the limits of this Moroccan resilience, linked in particular to the structure of its economic fabric, composed 90% of very small enterprises, a large proportion of which operate in the informal sector, exposing the country to structural risks of unpaid bills.

a3067.speaker: Coface (credit insurer)
a3067.name: Coface (credit insurer)
a3067.speech: Anticipates growth of +3.7% in 2025 for the African continent as a whole, driven mainly by the economies least dependent on raw materials and engaged in productive diversification ; also warns of energy uncertainties, particularly those linked to the Israel-Iran conflict and the threat of a blockage of the Strait of Hormuz, saying a surge in oil prices beyond 100 dollars a barrel cannot be ruled out, with significant repercussions for net importing countries such as Morocco and Tunisia, but also for the budgetary balances of producing countries such as Algeria and Libya.

a3158.speaker: Dr Jenfan Muswere, Minister of Information and Broadcasting Services
a3158.name: Dr Jenfan Muswere
a3158.title: Minister of Information and Broadcasting Services
a3158.speech: Said on Tuesday, addressing the 13th post cabinet media briefing, that the country had sold nearly 200 million kgs of tobacco by mid this month, an increase of 21 percent compared to the same period last year, when 151 million kg were sold ; “As of 16 May 2025, a total of 189 million kilogrammes of tobacco had been sold at an average price of US$3.38 per kilogramme. This represents a 21% increase in volume compared to the same period last season, when 151 million kilogrammes were sold at an average price of US$3.52 per Kilogramme.”

a3158.speaker: Dr Jenfan Muswere, Minister of Information and Broadcasting Services
a3158.name: Dr Jenfan Muswere
a3158.title: Minister of Information and Broadcasting Services
a3158.speech: Said with regards to the 2025 Winter Cereals Plan that the production targets are set at 600 000 metric tonnes of wheat from 120 000 hectares, 39 000 metric tonnes of barley from 6 500 hectares, and approximately 236 000 metric tonnes of potatoes from around 8 700 hectares.

a3158.speaker: Dr Jenfan Muswere, Minister of Information and Broadcasting Services
a3158.name: Dr Jenfan Muswere
a3158.title: Minister of Information and Broadcasting Services
a3158.speech: Said that according to the Second Round Crops, Livestock, and Fisheries Assessment (CLAFA) report of 12 April 2025, the country has adequate grain reserves at national level ; “In the interim, resources will be made available to the Grain Marketing Board (GMB) to facilitate timely payments for anticipated grain deliveries. The construction of 14 grain silo depots is making steady progress at 13 centres across the country, with the Kwekwe depot having been completed and officially commissioned by His Excellency the President, Dr. E.D. Mnangagwa.”

a3158.speaker: Second Round Crops, Livestock, and Fisheries Assessment (CLAFA) report of 12 April 2025
a3158.name: Second Round Crops
a3158.title: Livestock, and Fisheries Assessment (CLAFA) report of 12 April 2025
a3158.speech: Cited as showing that the country has adequate grain reserves at national level.

a3158.speaker: Dr Jenfan Muswere, Minister of Information and Broadcasting Services
a3158.name: Dr Jenfan Muswere
a3158.title: Minister of Information and Broadcasting Services
a3158.speech: Turning to this year’s cotton buying season, said it is set to begin on June 1, with prices per grade to be announced upon completion of ongoing consultations, and that to support the season’s operations preparations, including the establishment of 211 permanent buying points and 476 mobile buying points, have been completed.

a3347.speaker: 'Moea Makhakhe, Maseru City Council (MCC) Town Clerk
a3347.name: 'Moea Makhakhe
a3347.title: Maseru City Council (MCC) Town Clerk
a3347.speech: Said the collaboration with street vendors was important in that it would help maintain the cleanliness of Maseru's streets; said the five-year partnership with Alliance would allow them to efficiently manage waste disposal in the city. ; "We must work together to create a clean capital city with business opportunities for vendors and their families. This is not just an idea, it will happen, and today we are launching this initiative." ; Added that the initiative would span from Ha Hoohlo to Masianokeng and Masowe, ensuring that vendors earn a minimum wage while contributing to the city's cleanliness. ; "We have a project called 'Lefielo' where we spend M300 000 monthly to keep the city clean. I am negotiating with industry leaders to join this initiative. Every vendor should clean the streets before setting up their tables. It's not just about perception—vendors are vital in ensuring a clean environment, and it benefits them to maintain that cleanliness." ; Urged vendors to take responsibility for keeping their areas clean.

a3347.speaker: Limakatso Mokobocho, Alliance Insurance's Public Relations and Corporate Communications Manager
a3347.name: Limakatso Mokobocho
a3347.title: Alliance Insurance's Public Relations and Corporate Communications Manager
a3347.speech: Reiterated the company's long-standing commitment to giving back to the community. ; "In 2016, we launched the 'U Mang Policy,' aimed at creating a fund for each district from our profits. Although interrupted by COVID-19, we still managed to donate M1.5 million for vaccines." ; Added that through the U Mang initiative, Alliance had also provided M800 000 to help street vendors restart their businesses post-pandemic, and distributed M300 000 worth of food parcels to the less privileged during COVID-19. ; "Basotho have placed their trust in us for the past 30 years, and we are committed to giving back and supporting their livelihoods."

a3347.speaker: Alliance Insurance (company pledge)
a3347.name: Alliance Insurance (company pledge)
a3347.speech: Has committed to a significant investment aimed at keeping the city of Maseru clean, pledging to purchase two debris pickup trucks for the Maseru City Council, each valued at M1.7 million, as well as repair MCC parks, restore public toilets, and install shelters for street vendors.

a3351.speaker: United States (government announcement)
a3351.name: United States (government announcement)
a3351.speech: Said on Thursday that it will cut $50 million in annual aid to Zambia because of what it described as the "systemic theft" of donated drugs and medical supplies.

a3351.speaker: Michael Gonzales, US Ambassador to Zambia
a3351.name: Michael Gonzales
a3351.title: US Ambassador to Zambia
a3351.speech: Said the "difficult" decision comes after repeated warnings to the government to safeguard the vital medicines, which included life-saving drugs to treat malaria, HIV, and tuberculosis; said the US discovered in 2021 that medicine and medical supplies that were meant to be provided free to Zambians were being taken and sold by pharmacies across the country; said the Zambian government failed to do enough to address the corruption after being informed of the theft scandal last year; said the US was no longer willing to "underwrite the personal enrichment of fraudsters" with American taxpayers money; said he had recommended that the US start cutting the aid from January next year to give Zambia time to plan new procurements of the life-saving drugs.

a3351.speaker: Investigation of around 2,000 pharmacies in Zambia between 2021 and 2023
a3351.name: Investigation of around 2,000 pharmacies in Zambia between 2021 and 2023
a3351.speech: Found that nearly half of them were selling medicines and products paid for by US aid funds.

a3351.speaker: US Embassy in Zambia
a3351.name: US Embassy in Zambia
a3351.speech: Said it accounts for about a third of public health spending in the country.

a3351.speaker: Zambian government
a3351.name: Zambian government
a3351.speech: There was no immediate comment on Thursday from the Zambian government (non-response).

a3539.speaker: Ben Bernanke, economic historian of the Great Depression and former Federal Reserve Bank chair
a3539.name: Ben Bernanke
a3539.title: economic historian of the Great Depression and former Federal Reserve Bank chair
a3539.speech: “Economists still agree that Smoot-Hawley and the ensuing tariff wars were highly counterproductive and contributed to the depth and length of the global Depression.”

a3539.speaker: Paul Krugman, economist
a3539.name: Paul Krugman
a3539.title: economist
a3539.speech: Wrote that “Global trade agreements from the 1940s to the 1980s were used to bind democratic nations together during the Cold War, [and] Nafta was used to reward and encourage Mexican reformers.”

a3539.speaker: The Economist
a3539.name: The Economist
a3539.speech: Noted that “the same forces roiling American and European politics are also present in most of Asia: internal ethnic and communal tensions; protectionist fears about globalisation and job losses; and angry, assertive nationalism. India’s prime minister, Narendra Modi, seems unwilling or unable to control the extreme Hindu-nationalist wing of his own party; Shinzo Abe in Japan is similarly loath to distance himself definitively from his party’s right-wing historical revisionists; China’s Xi Jinping is encouraging a resurgence of national pride which can take ugly, xenophobic forms. All three play variations of Mr Trump’s rallying cry: ‘Make our country great again!’ The rise of nationalism at a time of economic gloom and geostrategic uncertainty is alarming for the region’s security. Europe, preoccupied with its own problems, has long forsaken any serious role in Asia. Now some Asians worry that America, needed more than ever to balance China and ensure the long peace, will start looking the other way.”

a3561.speaker: Local sources cited in the independent newsheet “Carta de Moçambique”
a3561.name: Local sources cited in the independent newsheet “Carta de Moçambique”
a3561.speech: Said all the victims were men; some of them were beheaded and others were shot dead while trying to flee the terrorists.

a3561.speaker: A source from the Balama district capital (anonymous)
a3561.name: A source from the Balama district capital (anonymous)
a3561.speech: “It all happened on the Messalo River. Balama lost four people, two of whom were murdered within Balama territory and two in the Montepuez area.”

a3561.speaker: Reports cited by AIM
a3561.name: Reports cited by AIM
a3561.speech: According to the reports, the other three victims were from Mavala Administrative Post; they were killed after the terrorists “attacked the villages of Messalo, Monapo, Nseue A, and Savamoto. The victims were buried in Balama.”

a3561.speaker: @DelgadoCabo (Cabo Delgado, social-media post, September 23, 2025)
a3561.name: @DelgadoCabo (Cabo Delgado
a3561.title: social-media post, September 23, 2025)
a3561.speech: “The insurgents are attacking, once again, today, in broad daylight, at the Mavala Administrative Post, in the #Balama district of Cabo Delgado.”

a3561.speaker: Doctors Without Borders (MSF) (statement)
a3561.name: Doctors Without Borders (MSF) (statement)
a3561.speech: Announced the temporary suspension of all its medical activities in the district of Mocímboa da Praia, “due to the worsening of armed violence in the region”: “The decision was made following a series of attacks this month that endangered the safety of civilians, health professionals, and medical infrastructure. The growing insecurity is drastically limiting the population’s access to essential health care. Hundreds of thousands of people urgently need medical and humanitarian assistance in Cabo Delgado, but insecurity continues to prevent them from receiving it” ; said the suspended activities include services in the Rural Hospital’s emergency room and maternity ward, emergency care, mental health support, and community outreach activities carried out by health workers in remote areas ; “Some patients requiring specialized care have been transferred to health facilities in Pemba and Mueda.”

a3561.speaker: International Organization for Migration (IOM)
a3561.name: International Organization for Migration (IOM)
a3561.speech: Said the total number of people displaced in recent attacks by terrorist groups in Cabo Delgado has risen to 5,770 in the districts of Muidumbe, Mocímboa da Praia and Montepuez.

a3561.speaker: IOM Mozambique (@IOM_Mozambique, social-media post, September 25, 2025)
a3561.name: IOM Mozambique (@IOM_Mozambique
a3561.title: social-media post, September 25, 2025)
a3561.speech: “Increased attacks & rising fear of violence by NSAG in Balama & Mocimboa da Praia districts have displaced over 3,600 people (19 – 22 Sep). Escalating violence underscores the urgent need for humanitarian aid & protection measures.”

a3735.speaker: Ursula von der Leyen, European Commission President
a3735.name: Ursula von der Leyen
a3735.title: European Commission President
a3735.speech: On South Africa as a partner: “The geopolitical ground is shifting beneath our feet, and we want to strengthen partnerships with trusted allies and friends. South Africa is such an ally and friend. Europe and South Africa are both vibrant democracies. We have both chosen unity in diversity. And we are both working toward a safer, more prosperous future for our people. More and more, we see the world through the same lens. We stand for a rules-based international order. We believe in the rule of law over the rule of force. We are like-minded in turbulent times. And that's precious. I know Europe can count on South Africa. And you can count on us.”

a3735.speaker: Ursula von der Leyen, European Commission President
a3735.name: Ursula von der Leyen
a3735.title: European Commission President
a3735.speech: On EU phytosanitary restrictions on SA citrus: “I know that this is an important issue. Like any other country, the EU has food and plant safety standards that are firmly grounded in science. In fact, our requirements are similar to those of other countries. The concerns raised by South Africa are currently being considered at the World Trade Organisation. I'm confident that a good solution that will benefit both Europe and South Africa will be found.”

a3735.speaker: Ursula von der Leyen, European Commission President
a3735.name: Ursula von der Leyen
a3735.title: European Commission President
a3735.speech: On foreign aid and Global Gateway: “The European Union is built in such a way that our member states have the power to decide how they spend their budgets. That's the case with the Netherlands. But you're right—the EU takes pride in its leadership in foreign aid because we know it's mutually beneficial. It builds strong partnerships. Take Global Gateway, Europe's investment plan for the world. We're investing €150 billion, almost R3 000 billion, into Africa alone. This is the next generation of foreign aid. We invest in high-quality, clean infrastructure, strategic industries, technology, and skills. And not just with grants. We also use our budget to de-risk and attract more public and private funding. It has a real impact. Global Gateway is already at work in South Africa. And more is coming. We have a new investment package for South Africa. With it, we will invest in clean energy projects... The package also includes new investments to boost vaccine and medication manufacturing to creating good jobs in this strategic industry. And finally, we're investing in connectivity, both physical and digital. That means transport corridors, like the North-South route from Durban to Lubumbashi. It means expanding fibre and 5G networks, connecting South Africa within and beyond.”

a3735.speaker: Ursula von der Leyen, European Commission President
a3735.name: Ursula von der Leyen
