a3735.title: European Commission President
a3735.speech: On European FDI in South Africa: “European foreign direct investment in South Africa amounts to more than €70 billion—almost R1 400 billion—a year. This is very significant. Today, more than 1 200 European companies operate in South Africa, fully complying with the laws in place, and providing jobs to over 300 000 South Africans. And I want to take our unique trade and investment further, so that more European companies come to South Africa and create good jobs for the people here.”

a3735.speaker: Ursula von der Leyen, European Commission President
a3735.name: Ursula von der Leyen
a3735.title: European Commission President
a3735.speech: On the EU versus other investors in Africa: “The EU is a fair and reliable partner. We base our partnerships on mutual respect and we have no hidden agendas. We promote a mutually beneficial approach... As great power competition intensifies, I see more countries wanting to engage with Europe. In the past months, we've concluded new partnerships with Mercosur, Mexico and Switzerland... And we are giving ourselves one year to conclude a free trade agreement with India. So why this appetite to engage with us? Because with us, what you see is what you get. We play by the rules - no hidden strings, no small print with big consequences, be it on local communities, the environment or even on a country's sovereignty. None of that with us. While others focus on extracting and exporting, we invest in local industries... In South Africa, we see major opportunities. We are discussing a future agreement on critical raw materials, but we're not just here to extract, from the pit to the port. We want to invest along the entire value chain, from exploration to recycling, creating local value and jobs. Our focus is on the industries of the future: green hydrogen, electric vehicles, and batteries.”

a3735.speaker: Ursula von der Leyen, European Commission President
a3735.name: Ursula von der Leyen
a3735.title: European Commission President
a3735.speech: Asked whether she knows where or what Lesotho is: “Of course, I know where Lesotho is. Europe has a diplomatic mission there and we are a long-standing partner of Lesotho and the Basotho people.”

a3944.speaker: USAID memorandum dated 4 February 2025, signed by Pete Morocco, deputy administrator for policy and planning
a3944.name: USAID memorandum dated 4 February 2025
a3944.title: signed by Pete Morocco, deputy administrator for policy and planning
a3944.speech: Placed USAID workers on forced administrative leave with pay until verdict, ordering them to be available by phone and email during normal working hours to respond to matters of urgency: “During the period that you are on administrative leave you are not to enter USAID premises, access USAID systems, or attempt to use your position or authority with USAID in any way without any prior permission or prior permission of a supervisor in your chain of command.”

a3944.speaker: USAID (announcement)
a3944.name: USAID (announcement)
a3944.speech: Recently announced that all USAID directly hired personnel globally would be placed on administrative leave, except designated personnel responsible for mission-critical functions, core leadership and specially designated programs.

a4128.speaker: Kuziemko and Werner (2006), research study
a4128.name: Kuziemko and Werner (2006)
a4128.title: research study
a4128.speech: Found that countries serving as non-permanent members of the UN Security Council receive more foreign aid from the UN and US-led agencies like UNICEF during their tenure.

a4341.speaker: Dr Philip Mpango, Vice-President of Tanzania
a4341.name: Dr Philip Mpango
a4341.title: Vice-President of Tanzania
a4341.speech: Outlined seven key measures to boost domestic revenue, including instructing tax collection agencies to intensify efforts in strengthening their revenue collection and management capacity; stressed the importance of accelerating efforts to reform the tax system to ensure equity and eliminate unproductive tax exemptions and concessions: "We must provide sufficient incentives for agents and institutions involved in tax collection to combat corrupt practices." ; instructed the relevant authorities to increase the use of ICT in tax collection, particularly by expanding the deployment of Electronic Fiscal Devices (EFDs), insisting that it is crucial to implement deliberate strategies to gradually reduce and ultimately eliminate dependence on foreign aid ; "We must also continue improving the business environment and enhancing investment."

a4341.speaker: Dr Philip Mpango, Vice-President of Tanzania
a4341.name: Dr Philip Mpango
a4341.title: Vice-President of Tanzania
a4341.speech: Underlined the need to build a robust taxpayer database, encompassing current and potential taxpayers, and to intensify efforts to increase the number of taxpayers; noted that the number of active domestic taxpayers had dropped from 3.36 million in 2021/2022 to 2.183 million in 2024/2025 ; "National demands are growing rapidly, with the population now reaching 65 million, the majority being youth. The current state of tax compliance calls for the development of comprehensive strategies to boost revenue." ; said that despite substantial efforts, tax compliance continues to face challenges, which impacts domestic revenue collection, and that many local government authorities have fallen short of their revenue targets, highlighting the need to enhance investment and business policies, regulations, and procedures ; "Therefore, this forum must engage in deep reflection and identify necessary improvements to broaden the tax base and enhance inclusivity."

a4341.speaker: Dr Saada Mkuya Salum, Zanzibar's Minister of State, President's Office - Finance and Planning
a4341.name: Dr Saada Mkuya Salum
a4341.title: Zanzibar's Minister of State, President's Office - Finance and Planning
a4341.speech: Said the government has continued to improve the investment environment to ensure active participation of the private sector in economic growth, having already eliminated nearly 380 investment-related bottlenecks; noted that through the forum the ministry will gather feedback to help refine strategies that increase citizen participation in economic development.

a4341.speaker: Stanslaus Nyongo, Deputy Minister in the President's Office for Planning and Investment
a4341.name: Stanslaus Nyongo
a4341.title: Deputy Minister in the President's Office for Planning and Investment
a4341.speech: Said the government has taken strong measures to improve the investment climate in the country; noted that 66 tax and investment laws had been amended, leading to the scrapping of hundreds of levies, and that the government has also enhanced digital registration systems across various regulatory bodies.

a4341.speaker: Elijah Mwandumbya, Deputy Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Finance
a4341.name: Elijah Mwandumbya
a4341.title: Deputy Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Finance
a4341.speech: Said that the Tax and Investment Dialogue was initiated three years ago, to bring together stakeholders to support the inclusive preparation of the national budget: "It is our norm to sit with stakeholders to ensure we incorporate their input so the budget reflects their needs. So far, in preparing the 2025/26 budget, we have already collected views from various zones." ; added that since July last year, the Tanzania Revenue Authority (TRA) has consistently surpassed its revenue collection targets, exceeding 100 per cent of its goals.

a4341.speaker: Angelina Ngalula, Chairperson of the Tanzania Private Sector Foundation (TPSF)
a4341.name: Angelina Ngalula
a4341.title: Chairperson of the Tanzania Private Sector Foundation (TPSF)
a4341.speech: Acknowledged the Ministry of Finance's leadership in implementing President Samia Suluhu Hassan's 4Rs (Reconciliation, Resilience, Reforms and Rebuilding) agenda in the financial and tax sectors; noted the ministry's efforts to streamline tax systems and ensure taxes are collected more efficiently, aligned with the president's vision of collecting taxes in a civilised, non-coercive manner, which has helped improve compliance.

a4341.speaker: Angelina Ngalula, Chairperson of the Tanzania Private Sector Foundation (TPSF)
a4341.name: Angelina Ngalula
a4341.title: Chairperson of the Tanzania Private Sector Foundation (TPSF)
a4341.speech: Stated that the forum was timely, coinciding with the drafting of the National Development Vision 2050, and considering the rapid pace of global technological change: "These global shifts call for us to change our mindsets and the way we do things. Given the mix of stakeholders present at this forum, we believe we will find a constructive path forward." ; added that there was an opportunity to add value to the country's agricultural products so that they could be exported directly to target countries, rather than relying on intermediaries ; underscored the need for education on the importance of paying taxes and formalising businesses, urging the Ministry of Finance's Research and Development unit to focus on public education ; recommended that the tax arbitration board be made independent and exclude TRA staff.

a4386.speaker: Oleksiy Goncharenko, Ukrainian member of parliament
a4386.name: Oleksiy Goncharenko
a4386.title: Ukrainian member of parliament
a4386.speech: In an interview granted to the American channel “CNN” last February, declared that Kyiv was ready to fight alongside Washington in any part of the world.

a4386.speaker: Tucker Carlson, American political writer and journalist
a4386.name: Tucker Carlson
a4386.title: American political writer and journalist
a4386.speech: Denounced in a book he wrote the crimes committed by the Ukrainian regime in several African countries such as Sudan, Mali and Chad, by fuelling conflict and creating instability through the sale of enormous quantities of American weapons to the rebel movements and terrorist groups active in those countries ; also expressed his concerns about the possibility that the Ukrainian authorities might sell biological weapons, obtained from American laboratories on their soil, to rebel and extremist movements in Africa, which could lead to a genuine disaster worldwide.

a4386.speaker: Sudanese and Arab media
a4386.name: Sudanese and Arab media
a4386.speech: Published numerous reports on the presence of Ukrainian forces and military experts specialising in the operation of drones within the ranks of the Rapid Support Forces.

a4386.speaker: Maxim Subkh, Ukraine’s special representative for Middle East and Africa affairs
a4386.name: Maxim Subkh
a4386.title: Ukraine’s special representative for Middle East and Africa affairs
a4386.speech: On 18 February, commenting on the participation of Ukrainian citizens in the fighting alongside Hemedti’s forces, declared: “Some Ukrainian citizens have chosen to participate unilaterally in the ongoing conflict in Sudan, most of them fight alongside the Rapid Support Forces, and some of them are technical specialists.”

a4386.speaker: Sudanese sources close to Hemedti, commander of the Rapid Support Forces (anonymous)
a4386.name: Sudanese sources close to Hemedti
a4386.title: commander of the Rapid Support Forces (anonymous)
a4386.speech: Indicated that Ukrainian military trainers and specialists had also taken part in training Chadian rebel movements in the Darfur region, close to the Chadian border, adding that Zelensky’s forces had sold a significant quantity of advanced weapons to these Chadian rebel forces.

a4386.speaker: High-level Chadian security sources (anonymous)
a4386.name: High-level Chadian security sources (anonymous)
a4386.speech: Last February warned of the presence of military reinforcements of the Chadian opposition in the border town of Tiné with Sudan, with the aim of launching imminent attacks against Chad, adding that this rebel force had obtained 600 combat vehicles.

a4386.speaker: Some security experts
a4386.name: Some security experts
a4386.speech: Consider that Kyiv would be responsible for the delivery of the advanced weapons obtained by the group “Boko Haram” over recent months, which has launched terrible attacks against the Chadian army and against villages bordering Nigeria.

a4386.speaker: Senior officials of the American administration
a4386.name: Senior officials of the American administration
a4386.speech: Confirmed that USAID was also involved in supporting and financing the terrorist group “Boko Haram” with the aim of destabilising several West African countries, including Chad.

a4386.speaker: Scott Perry, US Republican Representative of Pennsylvania
a4386.name: Scott Perry
a4386.title: US Republican Representative of Pennsylvania
a4386.speech: At the opening hearing of DOGE (Department of Government Effectiveness) held on 13 February, declared that USAID had financed the group “Boko Haram”, which has carried out terrorist attacks in Nigeria, Cameroon, Niger and Chad.

a4386.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4386.name: Donald Trump
a4386.title: US President
a4386.speech: According to President Trump’s statements, the sums the United States sent to Ukraine are estimated at 350 billion dollars.

a4386.speaker: Government of Kyiv (Ukraine)
a4386.name: Government of Kyiv (Ukraine)
a4386.speech: According to the government in Kyiv, Ukraine has received only 100 billion dollars from the United States and an additional 100 billion dollars from Europe and other partners.

a4525.speaker: Mutahi Kagwe, Kenyan Agriculture Cabinet Secretary
a4525.name: Mutahi Kagwe
a4525.title: Kenyan Agriculture Cabinet Secretary
a4525.speech: Has called upon the Common Market for East and Southern Africa (COMESA) to enforce a ban on hazardous pesticides across its member states, warning that the continued circulation of chemicals banned in some member states but permitted in others is compromising food safety, public health, and the integrity of regional agricultural trade: “The current situation where a pesticide banned in one country continues to be used next door completely undermines our collective SPS [Sanitary and Phytosanitary] efforts” ; “We are exposing our farmers, our consumers, and our markets to unnecessary and unacceptable risk” ; noted that the lack of consistency allowed unscrupulous traders to exploit gaps in enforcement, contributing to widespread contamination and the erosion of consumer trust in local and regional food systems ; “We must not let fragmented policies stand in the way of our people’s safety. Harmonising chemical standards is not optional, it is urgent.”

a4525.speaker: Kenya (delegation at the COMESA meeting)
a4525.name: Kenya (delegation at the COMESA meeting)
a4525.speech: Emphasised that effective regional food safety cannot exist without a common regulatory approach; other proposals from Kenya during the meeting included the sharing of agricultural technologies such as livestock vaccines, the development of protocols for cross-border trade in certified seeds, and digital innovations for agricultural planning.

a4525.speaker: Mutahi Kagwe, Kenyan Agriculture Cabinet Secretary
a4525.name: Mutahi Kagwe
a4525.title: Kenyan Agriculture Cabinet Secretary
a4525.speech: Reaffirmed Kenya’s commitment to supporting regional reforms, calling for bold leadership to transform COMESA from a “talk shop” into a functional platform for economic development, agricultural resilience, and food independence.

a4760.speaker: Quresho Adan Ishaq, widow and displaced mother in Baidoa camp
a4760.name: Quresho Adan Ishaq
a4760.title: widow and displaced mother in Baidoa camp
a4760.speech: “Our lives depended on the cash aid. We didn’t have to worry about food. I had a good life; my children were educated. We didn’t have to worry about anything. Now I feel like I’m exposed to the sun and standing in a lonely place, facing a tough life.” ; is upset that her children are now unable to continue at Koranic school as she can no longer pay the $15 monthly fees.

a4760.speaker: Abdi Mohamed Hassan, father of nine in Baidoa camp
a4760.name: Abdi Mohamed Hassan
a4760.title: father of nine in Baidoa camp
a4760.speech: “With the money, we used to buy enough food, which we don’t have now. Our lives became very difficult. I haven’t received any assistance from anyone for the past two months.”

a4760.speaker: Abdi Mohamed Hassan, father of nine in Baidoa camp
a4760.name: Abdi Mohamed Hassan
a4760.title: father of nine in Baidoa camp
a4760.speech: “We haven’t got any water from charity organisations for a long time, and no one has filled the water tanks. I don’t have money to buy water. How can we survive like this? We are in great trouble.”

a4760.speaker: Abdi Mohamed Hassan, father of nine in Baidoa camp
a4760.name: Abdi Mohamed Hassan
a4760.title: father of nine in Baidoa camp
a4760.speech: “Our current concern is that our children are no longer able to study. Five children were studying, but now they have returned to the neighbourhood. Their food is scarce, and they are not getting enough. The education of these children was very important to me, and now the children are just home in the neighbourhood, so I feel very sad for them.”

a4760.speaker: Said Osman Gabow, head of a family of 13 in Baidoa
a4760.name: Said Osman Gabow
a4760.title: head of a family of 13 in Baidoa
a4760.speech: “In the past, we used to manage our lives through aid and depended on it. Our daily lives were 100 percent stress-free, but now everything has changed. When aid stops, we are having a lot of trouble. It has made our lives difficult.”

a4760.speaker: Abdinasir Abdi Caruush, Minister of Relief for South West state
a4760.name: Abdinasir Abdi Caruush
a4760.title: Minister of Relief for South West state
a4760.speech: Warned that the humanitarian assistance provided in the state was intended to alleviate the problems faced by people displaced by conflict and drought, but was not planned to be a permanent fix.

a4830.speaker: Konrad Adenauer, Chancellor of West Germany (1951 address to Parliament)
a4830.name: Konrad Adenauer
a4830.title: Chancellor of West Germany (1951 address to Parliament)
a4830.speech: "... unspeakable crimes have been committed in the name of the German people, calling for moral and material indemnity ... The Federal Government are prepared, jointly with representatives of Jewry and the State of Israel ... to bring about a solution of the material indemnity problem, thus easing the way to the spiritual settlement of infinite suffering".

a4830.speaker: Joint Declaration between Namibia and Germany (document)
a4830.name: Joint Declaration between Namibia and Germany (document)
a4830.speech: insists on the version of Germany that what happened in 1904-1908 is only Genocide 'in today's terms'; does not delineate an effective comprehensive reparation to victims, does not spell out measures adopted to establish the truth about violations, and nowhere mentions the word Reparation; is silent on enlisting German companies who profited from forced labour and expropriations in Namibia to contribute towards indemnification.

a4830.speaker: Government of the Federal Republic of Germany
a4830.name: Government of the Federal Republic of Germany
a4830.speech: maintains the position - described by the author as untruths - that it cannot negotiate with non-state parties; acknowledged the genocide committed against the Ovaherero and Nama by Imperial Germany.

a4830.speaker: German Bundestag resolutions of 1989 and 2004
a4830.name: German Bundestag resolutions of 1989 and 2004
a4830.speech: are used in the Joint Declaration as justification for development assistance and reconciliation; the 1989 resolution is actually an agreement between Swapo and Germany, as initiated by Hans Dietrich Genscher, then German minister of foreign affairs.

a4830.speaker: UN Joint Communication from the Rapporteurs of the Special Procedures (February 2023)
a4830.name: UN Joint Communication from the Rapporteurs of the Special Procedures (February 2023)
a4830.speech: opined in no uncertain terms that the events of 1904-1908 were Genocide, and was emphatic that what must follow are reparations for the victims.

a4830.speaker: Namibian Parliament resolution of 2006 (from a motion tabled by the late Chief Kuaima Riruako, president of Nudo)
a4830.name: Namibian Parliament resolution of 2006 (from a motion tabled by the late Chief Kuaima Riruako
a4830.title: president of Nudo)
a4830.speech: provided the basis on which the genocide negotiations between Namibia and Germany ought to have been started; at the legislative level Namibia has already recognised that the atrocities of 1904-1908 were indeed Genocide.

a4830.speaker: The majority of Ovaherero/Nama organisations (OTA, NTLA, Okandjoze Chiefs' Assembly), political parties, church groups and prominent individuals from the Ovaherero and Nama communities
a4830.name: The majority of Ovaherero/Nama organisations (OTA
a4830.title: NTLA, Okandjoze Chiefs' Assembly), political parties, church groups and prominent individuals from the Ovaherero and Nama communities
a4830.speech: have rejected the Joint Declaration in toto.

a4971.speaker: Circuit Court in Accra, presided over by Susan Eduful
a4971.name: Circuit Court in Accra
a4971.title: presided over by Susan Eduful
a4971.speech: Remanded Charles Cobblah into police custody in connection with an alleged land fraud scheme, and ordered the prosecution to file all necessary disclosures and statements before the next hearing; the court has remanded him into police custody pending further proceedings.

a4971.speaker: Charles Cobblah, 55-year-old businessman (accused)
a4971.name: Charles Cobblah
a4971.title: 55-year-old businessman (accused)
a4971.speech: Pleaded not guilty to all charges; faces two counts of defrauding by false pretence, contrary to Section 131(1) of the Criminal Offences Act, 1960 (Act 29) and fraudulent transaction of land, contrary to Section 277(2) of the Land Act, 2020 (Act 1036).

a4971.speaker: Charles Cobblah, 55-year-old businessman (accused)
a4971.name: Charles Cobblah
a4971.title: 55-year-old businessman (accused)
a4971.speech: When confronted, admitted to reselling the land and promised a refund, which never materialised; during the investigation he confessed to the offence and refunded GH¢10,000.00, a fraction of the total sum.

a4971.speaker: Prosecution, led by DSP Evans Kesse
a4971.name: Prosecution
a4971.title: led by DSP Evans Kesse
a4971.speech: According to the facts presented by the prosecution, the complainant, Irene Esinam Tordjro, a businesswoman and the lawful attorney of her brother, Isaac Selorm Tordjro, was defrauded by Charles Cobblah in 2022; Cobblah allegedly demanded and received GH¢188,000.00 in cash and electrical appliances from Irene in exchange for two plots of land located at Kasoa-Ofaakor, valued at GH¢200,000.00, and promised to deliver the land documents after full payment.

a4971.speaker: Individual found developing the land (unnamed)
a4971.name: Individual found developing the land (unnamed)
a4971.speech: Claimed Cobblah had sold the same plots to him.

a5066.speaker: Joshua Aondongu Biem, Policy and Research Analyst at Nextier
a5066.name: Joshua Aondongu Biem
a5066.title: Policy and Research Analyst at Nextier
a5066.speech: Explained to Saturday INDEPENDENT that budget cuts are nothing new; however, where these cuts occur, the timing of such actions and the adjoining repercussions of such cuts remain key towards an economy's survival ; "Even though it has not been prioritised over the years, budgetary cuts are like kicking a dying horse, adding unnecessary pain to an already dire situation. Whether these cuts were made in good faith remains arguable, as it can be seen as a strategic decision to optimise limited resources." ; "On the flip side, it shows a lack of commitment to food security and poverty alleviation, which would only exacerbate a dire situation and have far-reaching impacts, especially on insecurity."

a5066.speaker: Joshua Aondongu Biem, Policy and Research Analyst at Nextier
a5066.name: Joshua Aondongu Biem
a5066.title: Policy and Research Analyst at Nextier
a5066.speech: Agreed, stating that allocating 10% of Nigeria's 2025 budget is undoubtedly important, because agricultural productivity would be boosted through modern farming tools and high-quality seeds, improving crop yield, and increased budget allocations could provide an avenue to expand credit facilities ; "This has been a major constraint for smallholder farmers in Nigeria. With an increased budget, farmers, including women farmers under organisations like SWOFON, can be opportune to scale up their production... a balanced strategy is best. Prioritising security to stabilise conflict-prone areas while strategically investing in agriculture to improve food security and generate jobs."

a5066.speaker: Hon. Ebube Ebisike-George, investment expert
a5066.name: Hon. Ebube Ebisike-George
a5066.title: investment expert
a5066.speech: Told the Saturday INDEPENDENT that the 36.19% cut in the 2025 budget from N996.901b in 2024 to N633b is definitely disturbing, and that the reduction being done in good faith is a testament to the All Progressive Congress (APC) government not being proactive and critically sensitive to the dire realities of Nigeria's population tittering on the brink of steadily growing massive hunger, deepening food insufficiency, depression, malnutrition and poverty ; "As it stands Nigeria relies on about $10 billion worth of imports to meet its food and agricultural production shortfalls (mostly wheat, rice, poultry, fish, food services, and consumer-oriented foods). Europe, Asia, the United States, South America, and South Africa are major sources of agricultural imports."

a5066.speaker: Tunde Banjoko, Chairman, Lagos Chambers of Commerce and Industry (LCCI) Agric and Agro-Allied Group
a5066.name: Tunde Banjoko
a5066.title: Chairman, Lagos Chambers of Commerce and Industry (LCCI) Agric and Agro-Allied Group
a5066.speech: Said that the initial proposed budget was N862bn which was about 1.1 percent of the entire budget ; "I am one of those that have always advocated that agriculture should get 10 per cent based on the Maputo/Malabo declaration which Nigeria also signed... Further reducing the cost of the budget shows that we will probably still be struggling with high cost of production, we will still be struggling with probably importing most of the produce we could have produced." ; "Our farmers will still be struggling with bad roads and high cost of production. So the effect of the reduction of that budget is going to be significant; we can see the budget of the livestock ministry is N11bn and they were looking at allocating about N380m to setting up the RUGA system. How would that have any effect compared to the current issue of farmer/herders clashes that we are experiencing?" ; "So, I think we should have prioritised increasing the number. The only time Nigeria ever witnessed anything significant in that industry was five per cent during President Yar'Adua for two years, 2008 and 2009; for the past years, it has been 1%, 1.2% that is why we have been advocating increase. I think the reduction is not in our favour and we should have done more in that regard."

a5066.speaker: Sunday Ezeobiora, National President of the Poultry Association of Nigeria (PAN) and Chairman of Sunchi Integrated Farms Limited
a5066.name: Sunday Ezeobiora
a5066.title: National President of the Poultry Association of Nigeria (PAN) and Chairman of Sunchi Integrated Farms Limited
a5066.speech: Said reducing the agricultural budget at this point of food insecurity in Nigeria will have several consequences on the agricultural sector and the country as a whole; said a decreased budget could lead to reduced investment in agriculture, potentially affecting food production and supply, impacting food security, leading to shortages and increased food prices, and that with less funding farmers may struggle to access essential resources like modern farming equipment, seeds, fertilizers, and technology; pointed out that this could result in decreased agricultural productivity and lower yields ; "Agriculture is a significant source of employment in Nigeria. A reduced budget may lead to fewer jobs in the sector, impacting livelihoods and contributing to unemployment rates. This could also have wider economic implications for the country." ; said a lower budget could mean reduced funding for research, innovation, and sustainable agricultural practices ; "In summary, reducing the agricultural budget for 2025 in Nigeria could have far-reaching consequences on food security, economic development, employment, rural communities, poverty levels, and the overall sustainability of the agricultural sector." ; said it is essential for the executive and legislators to carefully consider these implications and potentially explore ways to mitigate the effects of budget cuts on agriculture.

a5066.speaker: Sunday Ezeobiora, National President of the Poultry Association of Nigeria (PAN)
a5066.name: Sunday Ezeobiora
a5066.title: National President of the Poultry Association of Nigeria (PAN)
a5066.speech: Said he believes the reduction in Nigeria's agriculture budget could be attributed to various factors such as changes in government priorities, economic challenges, budget constraints, political decisions, or that the government is simply shifting focus to other sectors.

a5066.speaker: Sunday Ezeobiora, National President of the Poultry Association of Nigeria (PAN)
a5066.name: Sunday Ezeobiora
a5066.title: National President of the Poultry Association of Nigeria (PAN)
a5066.speech: Said allocating 10 per cent of the Nigerian 2025 budget to agriculture could have significant positive impacts on the agricultural sector and the economy as a whole; noted that a significant portion could be used to improve rural infrastructure, such as roads, irrigation systems, and storage facilities ; "Allocating funds for research and development in agriculture can lead to the adoption of modern farming techniques, improved seed varieties, and innovative tools that help increase yields and improve crop quality." ; "Investing in training programmes for farmers on sustainable agricultural practices, modern farming methods, and efficient use of resources can enhance their skills and knowledge, leading to higher productivity and income." ; "By allocating a portion of the budget to agricultural loans and financial support programmes for farmers, more farmers can have access to capital to expand their operations, purchase inputs, and invest in their farms." ; said supporting the development of markets for agricultural products through budgetary allocations can help farmers find better prices for their produce, reduce wastage, and promote agribusiness growth ; noted that both security and agriculture are very crucial for the well-being and development of Nigeria.

a5066.speaker: Fatimah Gumi, President of the Small-scale Women Farmers Organisation in Nigeria (SWOFON)
a5066.name: Fatimah Gumi
a5066.title: President of the Small-scale Women Farmers Organisation in Nigeria (SWOFON)
a5066.speech: At a press conference in Abuja, lamented that the federal government's commitment remains far below the 10% target set by the Malabo declaration; criticised the federal government's failure to prioritise agriculture, warning that the sector's underfunding could threaten Nigeria's food and nutrition security amid rising hunger and economic hardship.

a5066.speaker: Chi Tola-Robert, Chief Operating Officer of Capacious Farms and Foods
a5066.name: Chi Tola-Robert
a5066.title: Chief Operating Officer of Capacious Farms and Foods
a5066.speech: Pointed out the key consequences of the budget cut, stating that lower investment will surely reduce food production, increase prices, and worsen hunger; said it would also lead to job losses and rural poverty as millions depend on agriculture, and that there is no alternative to agriculture; said the reduction will also affect progress in mechanisation, irrigation, and research and will increase dependence on imports, stressing that weaker domestic production will heighten reliance on costly food imports; said the government may justify it due to economic constraints, debt servicing, or competing priorities such as security or infrastructure ; "However, if it harms food security, it could be seen as a short-sighted move or a misallocation of funds." ; said the Nigerian government should honour the Maputo declaration that recommends African nations allocate at least 10 per cent of their budgets to agriculture.

a5066.speaker: Femi Oke, Chairman of All Farmers Association of Nigeria (AFAN), Lagos state chapter
a5066.name: Femi Oke
a5066.title: Chairman of All Farmers Association of Nigeria (AFAN), Lagos state chapter
a5066.speech: Said that the amount budgeted for the sector will not be enough to cater for the sector, as there is a need to increase what was allocated; said it is just like a drop in the ocean, that the amount is grossly inadequate for developing agriculture in the country.

a5066.speaker: Henry Olatujoye, former national President of the National Palm Produce Association of Nigeria (NPPAN)
a5066.name: Henry Olatujoye
a5066.title: former national President of the National Palm Produce Association of Nigeria (NPPAN)
a5066.speech: Said that the reduction in the agriculture budget could be seen from different perspectives, "looking at it from last year's budget, it is easy to believe that it will not be good for agricultural development and further putting pressure on agric practices, commodity development, and other value chains"; said reducing the budget this year by 36 per cent is a reflection of the total investment and commitment achieved in the year 2024; noted that the Federal Government did a lot in the area of insecurity, inputs, supplies, access to land, and commodity trading ; "It is no longer news that Nigeria's agricultural sector has been hurt by several shocks which in the last 10 years of APC rule have a toll on the wellbeing of its citizens and economy. These are regular flooding, desertification of crop and grazing land, armed extremist insurgencies which have been linked to USAID funding now deactivated by President Trump, as well as conflicts between herdsmen and local farmers which has seriously destroyed food production and Herdsmen Militia actions been linked to land grabbing." ; "The onslaught of foreign Agribusiness behemoths like Dupont, Monsanto and co. who continue to push GMO seeds can further hurt the fragile state of Africa's organic agricultural process which needs urgent mechanisation... food processing continues to suffer from a lack of financing and infrastructure. These challenges have exacerbated food inflation." ; explained that reducing the 2025 agriculture budget means "reduced food productivity and availability in the farming/Agribusiness sector which is already plagued by corruption and other hurdles. In effect malnourishment and hunger will increase." ; "The consequences of this significant budget cut are likely to be severe. Lower funding translates to decreased investment in research, extension services, improved seeds, fertilizers, irrigation, and farm mechanisation. This directly impacts agricultural productivity, leading to lower yields and reduced food availability."

a5066.speaker: NIMET (Nigerian Meteorological Agency)
a5066.name: NIMET (Nigerian Meteorological Agency)
a5066.speech: "NIMET has predicted early rains this year, which means farmers will have the opportunity to plant crops such as maize and other grains twice this year."

a5294.speaker: Ola Olukoyede, Chairman of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC)
a5294.name: Ola Olukoyede
a5294.title: Chairman of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC)
a5294.speech: announced the conviction and sentencing of 146 out of 194 foreign nationals arrested in connection with cybersecurity-related financial crimes in Nigeria; the 146 foreigners would serve their jail terms before being repatriated to their country. "Last year, we arrested about 194 foreigners who were involved in various forms of financial crimes and activities that are inimical to the economic growth and development of our country. Today, I can tell you that we have succeeded in prosecution and conviction of 146 of them. They will serve their jail terms and will be repatriated to their respective countries."

a5294.speaker: Ola Olukoyede, EFCC Chairman
a5294.name: Ola Olukoyede
a5294.title: EFCC Chairman
a5294.speech: praised the FBI, Interpol and other international security institutions for their support in ensuring successful prosecution of the cyber criminals.

a5294.speaker: Ola Olukoyede, EFCC Chairman
a5294.name: Ola Olukoyede
a5294.title: EFCC Chairman
a5294.speech: said the EFCC would soon inaugurate a Cybersecurity Centre in its facility with the capability to detect and respond to Cybersecurity attacks within one hour, stressing that Cybersecurity attacks relating to financial crimes are becoming more organised across the world ; said it had become imperative for security institutions and agencies as well as banks and regulatory bodies to collaborate to combat cyber crimes, saying the EFCC would soon commission a 500-capacity Research Centre for reformation and rehabilitation of convicted cyber criminals.

a5294.speaker: Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) (statement released Tuesday)
a5294.name: Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) (statement released Tuesday)
a5294.speech: stated that its operatives from the Kaduna Zonal Directorate arrested nine suspected illegal miners in Kaniyan Village, Mokwa Local Government Area, Niger State; the arrest followed the receipt of actionable intelligence regarding ongoing illegal mining operations in the area.

a5294.speaker: SaharaReporters
a5294.name: SaharaReporters
a5294.speech: reported [a day earlier] that the EFCC stated that its operatives from the Kaduna Zonal Directorate arrested nine suspected illegal miners in Kaniyan Village, Mokwa Local Government Area, Niger State.

a5325.speaker: Michael J. Adler, U.S. Ambassador to South Sudan (press statement)
a5325.name: Michael J. Adler
a5325.title: U.S. Ambassador to South Sudan (press statement)
a5325.speech: Announced in a press statement on Monday the arrival of USAID Mission Director for South Sudan David Thompson, who assumed the position on 1st October.

a5410.speaker: David Silinde, Tanzanian Deputy Minister of Agriculture
a5410.name: David Silinde
a5410.title: Tanzanian Deputy Minister of Agriculture
a5410.speech: Said the Government will continue to work with stakeholders to invest in the agriculture sector through strategic projects under the Building a Better Tomorrow (BBT) Programme ; “The great efforts being made by the Government in collaboration with private sector stakeholders have brought great success in adding value to crops, along with USAID’s participation through the Feed the Future project.” ; “The Government has invested in large farms through the BBT project; Chunya District, Mbeya Region, has set aside 57,000 acres for agriculture.”

a5410.speaker: David Silinde, Tanzanian Deputy Minister of Agriculture
a5410.name: David Silinde
a5410.title: Tanzanian Deputy Minister of Agriculture
a5410.speech: Asked agricultural stakeholders to increase their efforts to reach more young people in the areas where large farms have been invested in for the implementation of the BBT programme, and encouraged young people to use the opportunities offered by the agriculture sector, stressing that the Mbeya and Songwe regions have been the centre of the Ministry of Agriculture in the production of food and cash crops.

a5410.speaker: Jumanne Sanga, Executive Director of Kibanza Company
a5410.name: Jumanne Sanga
a5410.title: Executive Director of Kibanza Company
a5410.speech: Said 502 young people have been given training in product processing as well as education on climate change and the efficient use of moisture in production ; said the aim is to enable young people to add value to their crops and to use various methods to cope with the challenges of climate change.

a5410.speaker: Mariam Mkisi, beneficiary of the project (chilli processor)
a5410.name: Mariam Mkisi
a5410.title: beneficiary of the project (chilli processor)
a5410.speech: Said the project has helped her to be connected to large domestic and foreign markets for the distribution of her products.

a5445.speaker: Citizens of Maryland County speaking on a local radio talk show
a5445.name: Citizens of Maryland County speaking on a local radio talk show
a5445.speech: Speaking on a local radio talk show in the county, many citizens, in anger, wondered whether the Government of Liberia, through the Ministry of Public Works, is concerned about Liberians' safety and free movement. According to them, such a great occasion that will bring relief to peoples of both countries, attended by representatives from ECOWAS, SHAANXI Construction Engineering Corporation LTD, and Engineers from Côte d'Ivoire, was held without the presence of Minister Giddings or any representative of the Ministry of Public Works ; the citizens termed Minister Giddings's response embarrassing because they were looking forward to seeing him perform at the event, as it would've drawn the attention of ECOWAS and Chinese engineers gearing up for the project ; according to them, despite their excitement and anticipation, the Public Works Ministry was nowhere around, which they described as worrisome and questionable.

a5445.speaker: Roland Giddings, Liberian Minister of Public Works (relayed through ECOWAS Project Manager Ashok Maliki)
a5445.name: Roland Giddings
a5445.title: Liberian Minister of Public Works (relayed through ECOWAS Project Manager Ashok Maliki)
a5445.speech: Contacted during the opening of the program as to why he had not arrived when his Ivorian counterparts were already present at the occasion, responded that he was stuck in the mud near Nimbia County in Liberia.

a5445.speaker: Pastor Abraham Togba, resident of Zone 7A and caller on the radio talk show
a5445.name: Pastor Abraham Togba
a5445.title: resident of Zone 7A and caller on the radio talk show
a5445.speech: Laments that the absence of Liberian officials at such a great occasion wasn't only embarrassing but disgraceful to the entire country because President Boakai can't be everywhere and that's why he appointed cabinet ministers to fill such gap, but notes that to have heard the Minister saying he wasn't present because his vehicle stuck in the mud, was a big shame ; adds that such an excuse was very poor, stressing that Giddings had been invited and informed about the event days before the ceremony ; “So the Minister who should've had the roads fixed is crying of being stuck; what happens to ordinary Liberians that use the roads on a daily basis?” ; continues that Liberians will now begin to notice the change they made in the poll, whether it's positive or negative, adding that it's so early for people to start criticizing the government for not attending important events.

a5445.speaker: Jerryling Geetah, caller from Zone 11
a5445.name: Jerryling Geetah
a5445.title: caller from Zone 11
a5445.speech: “I can't believe that the Public Works Ministry or Minister didn't show up. We have been praying tirelessly for years to make this event a success, and he couldn't even spare a few hours to unbrace such a great occasion.” ; explains that there are reasons why such things are happening in Liberia, such as people's unwillingness to correct wrongs; points out that even in the Minister's absence, the County Resident Engineer should have shown up, pointing out that the program wasn't held secretly or behind closed doors ; believes that Liberian officials didn't turn out only because ECOWAS did not bring money to share, noting that had that been the case, the entire place would've been filled with Liberian officials ; calls on President Boakai to take such occasions seriously and take action against officials who downplay them because this could undermine his government's growth and development ; “So to say, we are watching because we will not allow any government officials to stop our progress and developments. Other countries are moving forward, and we are still behind due to some officials' attitudes.”

a5445.speaker: Jacob Towliad, supporter of the ruling Unity Party and public school teacher
a5445.name: Jacob Towliad
a5445.title: supporter of the ruling Unity Party and public school teacher
a5445.speech: Criticizes the Public Works Minister's absence: “I thought Minister Giddings would've come for sure because road connectivity has always been his involvement and activities. I can't believe he has made such a statement.” ; maintains that, given the importance attached to the project, it was prudent that the Minister should've taken a flight to Maryland, as he claimed the roads were bad ; “Let me say, it was a failure on the part of the Minister and the local officials of the county because their presence was very important during such an occasion.”

a5445.speaker: Chris Appiah, Acting Director of Transport of the ECOWAS Commission
a5445.name: Chris Appiah
a5445.title: Acting Director of Transport of the ECOWAS Commission
a5445.speech: Disclosed that official groundbreaking for the project will be done hopefully in November this year and is expected to bring together the Presidents of both countries when the Public Works Minister may attend ; says the bridge project is an ECOWAS Commission's initiative through its President in collaboration with the African Development Bank as a way of giving back to 400 million people living within the West African region.

a5526.speaker: Zhao Jiangping, Ambassador of China to Burundi (opinion article)
a5526.name: Zhao Jiangping
a5526.title: Ambassador of China to Burundi (opinion article)
a5526.speech: Wrote that on 31 July 2025, thanks to close cooperation between the governments and enterprises of Burundi and China, the first batch of 38.4 tonnes of Burundian arabica coffee beans was successfully shipped to China, the first direct export of Burundian coffee beans to the Chinese market and an important milestone in Burundian products gaining the benefit of zero-tariff treatment; enterprises on both sides subsequently signed purchase contracts for more than 900 tonnes of Burundian coffee beans worth more than 5 million US dollars, testifying to the Chinese market’s strong recognition of the quality of Burundian coffee.

a5526.speaker: Zhao Jiangping, Ambassador of China to Burundi
a5526.name: Zhao Jiangping
a5526.title: Ambassador of China to Burundi
a5526.speech: Said this first shipment testifies to the concrete implementation of China’s commitments towards Africa; “China always remains the African continent’s reliable development partner”, and faced with a global context marked by uncertainty, China continues to promote openness and win-win cooperation and works towards building a high-level China-Africa community of shared future ; noted that since 1 December 2024 China has granted zero-tariff treatment to 100% of products exported to China by the least developed countries, including 33 African countries, becoming the first developing country and first major economy to apply such a measure, and that in June 2025 China announced the zero-tariff policy on 100% of taxable products for the 53 African countries having diplomatic relations with it.

a5526.speaker: Zhao Jiangping, Ambassador of China to Burundi
a5526.name: Zhao Jiangping
a5526.title: Ambassador of China to Burundi
a5526.speech: “As a Chinese proverb says, ‘One must look far ahead in order to advance better’”; said China wishes to work hand in hand with Burundi to promote high-quality cooperation within the Belt and Road Initiative and to implement the “Ten partnership actions for jointly promoting modernisation”; invited Burundian enterprises to seize the opportunities offered by the China International Import Expo, the China-Africa Economic and Trade Expo and the Silk Road e-commerce platforms so that Burundian products can truly “enter, remain and sell well” in China.

a5592.speaker: Economic analysts
a5592.name: Economic analysts
a5592.speech: Expressed fears that the temporary ban on foreign [aid] imposed by the US government could worsen the forex shortages the country is experiencing in the short to medium term ; observed that the pause, if prolonged, could deepen economic instability.

a5592.speaker: US government
a5592.name: US government
a5592.speech: Announced that President Donald Trump's administration has paused all foreign assistance funded by or through the State Department and United States Agency for International Development pending review.

a5592.speaker: Greenson Nyirenda, Catholic University economics lecturer
a5592.name: Greenson Nyirenda
a5592.title: Catholic University economics lecturer
a5592.speech: Said the loss could worsen the country's forex crisis: "The funding by international organisations remains one of the significant sources of forex for countries like Malawi that have low exportation capacity. This will hit hard."

a5592.speaker: Velli Nyirongo, Scotland-based Malawian economist
a5592.name: Velli Nyirongo
a5592.title: Scotland-based Malawian economist
a5592.speech: Warned that the reduced forex availability could strain reserves, weaken the government's ability to meet external obligations, and destabilise the exchange rate: "Over time, sustained aid withdrawal may exacerbate fiscal imbalances, forcing the government to seek alternative financing through increased borrowing or expanded export earnings, both of which may take time to materialise," he said in a WhatsApp response ; further said policy makers may need to tighten monetary policy, diversify export earning, strengthen remittance inflows, and secure alternative funding from multilateral institutions or regional trade agreements.

a5592.speaker: Reserve Bank of Malawi (figures)
a5592.name: Reserve Bank of Malawi (figures)
a5592.speech: Figures show that total forex reserves had dropped to $516.9 million (2.1 months of imports) at the end of November 2024, far below the 3.9 months of import cover recommended by multilateral institutions such as the World Bank and the IMF, and lower than the $568.9 million (2.3 months of imports) recorded in November 2023.

a5637.speaker: Omar Hilale, Moroccan Ambassador (cited by Al Ahdath Al Maghribia)
a5637.name: Omar Hilale
a5637.title: Moroccan Ambassador (cited by Al Ahdath Al Maghribia)
a5637.speech: Recalled, in Awaza, Turkmenistan, that under the impetus of King Mohammed VI, Rabat actively supports landlocked African countries through South-South and triangular projects intended to promote regional integration and investment.

a5637.speaker: Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Burkina Faso (in Rissalat Al Oumma)
a5637.name: Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré
a5637.title: Minister of Foreign Affairs of Burkina Faso (in Rissalat Al Oumma)
a5637.speech: Welcomed this initiative as a source of inspiration for Sahel states’ access to the Atlantic.

a5637.speaker: Libération (newspaper)
a5637.name: Libération (newspaper)
a5637.speech: Reports that American President Donald Trump reaffirmed Washington’s recognition of Moroccan sovereignty over the Sahara.

a5637.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
a5637.name: Donald Trump
a5637.title: President of the United States
a5637.speech: Reaffirmed Washington’s recognition of Moroccan sovereignty over the Sahara.

a5637.speaker: Ricardo Sanchez Serra, Peruvian journalist
a5637.name: Ricardo Sanchez Serra
a5637.title: Peruvian journalist
a5637.speech: Describes it as a “historic alliance” between Rabat and Washington.

a5637.speaker: Ahmed Assaf, Palestinian minister (cited by Al Ittihad Al Ichtiraki)
a5637.name: Ahmed Assaf
a5637.title: Palestinian minister (cited by Al Ittihad Al Ichtiraki)
a5637.speech: Welcomed the humanitarian and medical aid sent by King Mohammed VI to Gaza, insisting on its direct impact on the population.

a5637.speaker: Annahar Al Maghribia (newspaper)
a5637.name: Annahar Al Maghribia (newspaper)
a5637.speech: Notes that Moroccan pension schemes collected 66.8 billion dirhams in 2024 (+8.9%), paying out 71.1 billion in benefits, with reserves close to 327 billion.

a5637.speaker: TSA (news outlet)
a5637.name: TSA (news outlet)
a5637.speech: Reports that after France suspended visa exemptions, Algiers denounced any form of pressure and announced reciprocal measures affecting visas and real estate.

a5637.speaker: Algerian government (Algiers)
a5637.name: Algerian government (Algiers)
a5637.speech: Denounced any form of pressure and announced reciprocal measures affecting visas and real estate.

a5637.speaker: L’Expression (newspaper)
a5637.name: L’Expression (newspaper)
a5637.speech: Reports that the East African Community has launched the “EAC Bond,” a single customs bond mechanism meant to smooth intra-African trade and perceived as a tool strengthening integration.

a5637.speaker: APS (Algerian press agency)
a5637.name: APS (Algerian press agency)
a5637.speech: Indicates that Algeria has issued a call to national talent and to its diaspora to create an expertise council dedicated to developing an integrated mechanical industry.

a5637.speaker: La Presse (newspaper)
a5637.name: La Presse (newspaper)
a5637.speech: Announces that declared investments in Tunisia rose by 16.9% over six months, reaching 3.3 billion Tunisian dinars, supported by a 300-million-dinar tourism project in Jendouba.

a5637.speaker: Tunisie Numérique (news outlet)
a5637.name: Tunisie Numérique (news outlet)
a5637.speech: Notes that domestic demand is collapsing, holding up only thanks to transfers from Tunisians abroad, in a context of soaring prices.

a5637.speaker: La Presse (newspaper)
a5637.name: La Presse (newspaper)
a5637.speech: Reports the release of the regional director of National Security of Nabeul after a week in detention as part of an investigation.

a5637.speaker: eanlibya.com (news outlet)
a5637.name: eanlibya.com (news outlet)
a5637.speech: Reports that Tripoli and Algiers are discussing the strengthening of bilateral relations in various fields, with an emphasis on regional matters of common interest.

a5637.speaker: eanlibya.com (news outlet)
a5637.name: eanlibya.com (news outlet)
a5637.speech: Indicates that Libya and the UN have agreed on partnerships for the implementation of the Sustainable Development Goals, including financial inclusion and environmental resilience.

a5637.speaker: eanlibya.com (news outlet)
a5637.name: eanlibya.com (news outlet)
a5637.speech: Specifies that Libyan soldiers took part in the “Africa Peace 3” exercise organised by Algeria to improve peacekeeping capacities.

a5637.speaker: gomhuriaonline (news outlet)
a5637.name: gomhuriaonline (news outlet)
a5637.speech: Reports the signing of a protocol between the Libyan ministries of Transport and Religious Endowments to promote road safety and civic values.

a5637.speaker: egyptindependent (news outlet)
a5637.name: egyptindependent (news outlet)
a5637.speech: Reports that Donald Trump has imposed a 10% customs duty on Egyptian imports, affecting five major categories of exports, a measure likely to directly impact Cairo’s trade balances.

a5772.speaker: Alexandre Monteiro, Cabo Verdean Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy
a5772.name: Alexandre Monteiro
a5772.title: Cabo Verdean Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy
a5772.speech: Stated at a press conference on Friday that the Government is working to restore normal electricity supply in Santiago, but without committing to concrete deadlines: “We are not committing to dates” for resolving the energy problems.

a5772.speaker: Alexandre Monteiro, Cabo Verdean Minister of Energy
a5772.name: Alexandre Monteiro
a5772.title: Cabo Verdean Minister of Energy
a5772.speech: Told Lusa that the projects under the debt-for-climate-investment swap agreement with Portugal are advancing, stressing that the climate and environment fund has already been legally created.

a5772.speaker: Alexandre Monteiro, Cabo Verdean Minister of Energy
a5772.name: Alexandre Monteiro
a5772.title: Cabo Verdean Minister of Energy
a5772.speech: Estimated that Cabo Verde expects to save almost double on fuel with the increase in renewables — in 2023 the country saved almost 2 million contos — and said Cabo Verde wants to achieve 100% access to electricity by 2026.

a5772.speaker: Alexandre Monteiro, Cabo Verdean Minister of Energy
a5772.name: Alexandre Monteiro
a5772.title: Cabo Verdean Minister of Energy
a5772.speech: Assured that “Projects already exceed the 30% renewable energy penetration foreseen for 2026,” that investments in renewable energy and the energy transition will allow a 22% reduction in fossil fuel consumption in electricity production, and announced that the government is studying the possibility of increasing incentives for the purchase of electric-motor taxis; the Government obtained financing for projects in the National Energy Sustainability Programme, one of them a pump-and-storage station to be built in the municipality of Ribeira Grande de Santiago, budgeted at around 70 million euros.

a5772.speaker: Israel Katz, Israeli Minister of Energy
a5772.name: Israel Katz
a5772.title: Israeli Minister of Energy
a5772.speech: Warned that his country will not allow the entry of essential goods or humanitarian aid into Gaza until Hamas releases the people kidnapped on Saturday in Israel: “Aid to Gaza? No switch will be turned on until the kidnapped return.”

a5772.speaker: Cabo Verdean Minister of Energy
a5772.name: Cabo Verdean Minister of Energy
a5772.speech: Announced at a press conference the measures to mitigate the rise in fuel prices: prices of gas and fuel for electricity production frozen, petrol and diesel with a maximum increase of 5%.

a5772.speaker: Government of Cabo Verde
a5772.name: Government of Cabo Verde
a5772.speech: Guarantees that it is monitoring the situation and that it will assess the “available instruments” to reduce the impacts that the rise in oil prices on international markets, driven by the war in Ukraine, will have on Cabo Verde, and wants to be prepared to “mitigate the situation.”

a5772.speaker: Cabo Verdean Minister of Energy
a5772.name: Cabo Verdean Minister of Energy
a5772.speech: Assured, after meeting with companies in the energy sector to analyse the impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic on the national energy sector, that recovery in the fuel and electricity sector will take place as consumption returns to normal.

a5772.speaker: Cabo Verdean Minister of Industry, Commerce and Energy
a5772.name: Cabo Verdean Minister of Industry
a5772.title: Commerce and Energy
a5772.speech: Guaranteed that the World Bank technical assistance with a view to the privatisation of the water and power company Electra starts this month.

a5772.speaker: Cabo Verdean Minister of Industry, Commerce and Energy
a5772.name: Cabo Verdean Minister of Industry
a5772.title: Commerce and Energy
a5772.speech: Said on Wednesday that the privatisation of Electra will not happen this year, but admitted that the technical support work is being prepared to be presented to the Government; the privatisation process “is proceeding normally.”

a5772.speaker: Alexandre Monteiro, Cabo Verdean Minister of Energy
a5772.name: Alexandre Monteiro
a5772.title: Cabo Verdean Minister of Energy
a5772.speech: Took stock, a year after the start of the government’s new energy plan, of what has been done and what lies ahead, saying that micro-generation is growing and is “the right bet.”

a6022.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, President of France
a6022.name: Emmanuel Macron
a6022.title: President of France
a6022.speech: Said he told Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Tuesday 15 April that "the ordeal" of Gaza's civilians must "come to an end", calling for a ceasefire allowing the release of the Hamas hostages and for "the opening of all humanitarian aid crossing points" ; "Ceasefire, release of all hostages, humanitarian aid, then finally the reopening of a prospect of a political two-State solution. It is in this context that I envisage the June Conference" which France will co-chair at the UN, "taking into account the security interests of Israel and of everyone in the region" ; "The ordeal being endured by the civilian populations of Gaza must come to an end" ; "The opening of all humanitarian aid crossing points is a vital necessity for the civilian populations of Gaza. I saw it at El-Arish: this aid is blocked on the other side of the border. It must reach civilians as quickly as possible" ; Repeated that "the ceasefire is the only way to ensure the release of the hostages still held by Hamas" and affirmed that "the release of all hostages has always been an absolute priority, as has the demilitarisation of Hamas."

a6022.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli Prime Minister (statement from his office)
a6022.name: Benjamin Netanyahu
a6022.title: Israeli Prime Minister (statement from his office)
a6022.speech: Told Emmanuel Macron that the establishment of a Palestinian State would be "an enormous reward for terrorism", his office indicated: "During the conversation, the Prime Minister firmly opposed the creation of a Palestinian State, saying that it would constitute an enormous reward for terrorism."

a6024.speaker: Aissa Laouan Wandarama, Minister of Humanitarian Action and Disaster Management of Niger
a6024.name: Aissa Laouan Wandarama
a6024.title: Minister of Humanitarian Action and Disaster Management of Niger
a6024.speech: Officially launched the ceremony on behalf of the government and paid tribute "to the courage of those who risk their lives to help the most destitute", saying the day is also an occasion to highlight the resilience and above all the generosity of local communities, which in times of crisis are the first to bring relief to people in distress: "These communities deserve the respect and consideration of the entire humanitarian community, and must for that reason be celebrated."

a6024.speaker: Harouna Zakou, Deputy Country Director of Pathfinder International in Niger
a6024.name: Harouna Zakou
a6024.title: Deputy Country Director of Pathfinder International in Niger
a6024.speech: "I would like to take this opportunity to join the entire great humanitarian family in celebrating the courage, the determination and the commitment of all the actors who fight every day to bring positive changes to the lives of Nigerien communities alongside the national authorities." ; "We pay tribute to all the humanitarian actors who fight every day so that the most vulnerable populations can benefit from basic social services and improve their living conditions. We also pay tribute to all those who brave, day after day, the difficulties in the field and the many risks to which they are exposed. We are in the rainy season, with roads that are cut off, but despite this there are men and women who fight with determination to bring health care services, economic and livelihood support to the vulnerable populations affected by the scourges and difficulties of life. We say bravo to these actors and congratulate them on their commitment." ; Also saluted and congratulated all the "Pathfinders" in Niger and around the world who are committed day after day to going beyond barriers and providing essential health care services to the most destitute populations.

a6024.speaker: Harouna Zakou, Deputy Country Director of Pathfinder International in Niger
a6024.name: Harouna Zakou
a6024.title: Deputy Country Director of Pathfinder International in Niger
a6024.speech: "Pathfinder, as a member of this great humanitarian and development family, has been working alongside the government and the Nigerien authorities for more than 10 years to provide access to primary health care, to maternal, newborn and child health services, and to quality reproductive health and family planning services, for the women and young people of Niger." ; To conclude his address, renewed the international organisation's commitment to continuing its activities and its support to the government of Niger in order to strengthen the resilience of women, young people and the most vulnerable populations in Niger.

a6051.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a6051.name: Marco Rubio
a6051.title: US Secretary of State
a6051.speech: Announced that the vast majority of USAID's programmes have been terminated after a six-week purge; on X, said that the initiatives “spent tens of billions in ways that did not serve” or harmed US interests ; said that after the review, the US was “officially ending” about 5,200 of USAID's 6,200 programmes ; “In consultation with Congress, we intend for the remaining 18% of programmes we are keeping....to be administered more effectively under the State Department” ; thanked Doge and State Department staff “who worked very long hours to achieve this overdue and historic reform”.

a6051.speaker: Humanitarian organisations around the world
a6051.name: Humanitarian organisations around the world
a6051.speech: Have warned that the controversial move to end long-running US aid programmes is already having dire consequences around the world, potentially endangering lives.

a6051.speaker: The Trump administration
a6051.name: The Trump administration
a6051.speech: Has repeatedly made clear that it wants overseas spending to be closely aligned with its “America First” approach.

a6051.speaker: Democrats and various humanitarian organisations
a6051.name: Democrats and various humanitarian organisations
a6051.speech: Have characterised the shutdown of USAID's programmes – which were funded by Congress – as illegal, prompting several lawsuits.

a6104.speaker: United Nations (2024)
a6104.name: United Nations (2024)
a6104.speech: "One woman or girl is killed every 10 minutes"

a6104.speaker: Women's Land and Resource Rights (WLR2) Platform
a6104.name: Women's Land and Resource Rights (WLR2) Platform
a6104.speech: Urges greater attention and action to address GBV in Zambia's natural resource management sectors during the 2024 16 Days of Activism Against GBV.

a6104.speaker: Samantha Munang'andu, RISE Project Coordinator at Action Aid Zambia
a6104.name: Samantha Munang'andu
a6104.title: RISE Project Coordinator at Action Aid Zambia
a6104.speech: "GBV is not just physical. It affects every aspect of a woman's life, lowering her self-esteem, hampering her performance in leadership roles, and denying her economic opportunities. By championing the rights of women, I shine light on the critical need for GBV prevention in the fisheries sector."

a6104.speaker: Maina Malaya, Communications Officer, Wildlife Crime Prevention (WCP)
a6104.name: Maina Malaya
a6104.title: Communications Officer, Wildlife Crime Prevention (WCP)
a6104.speech: "Zambia's wildlife management has made strides in addressing GBV by increasing women's participation in roles like community scouts and conservation leaders. However, cultural resistance and limited access to leadership positions hinder progress and perpetuate GBV risks. During these 16 days of activism, I recommit to creating safe spaces for women, equipping them to excel in their roles, and fostering understanding among men to support women as indispensable allies"

a6104.speaker: Monje Sabela Siyeni, Women's Land and Resource Rights Platform Coordinator
a6104.name: Monje Sabela Siyeni
a6104.title: Women's Land and Resource Rights Platform Coordinator
a6104.speech: "Gender based violence affects both women and men, but when GBV is related to land, it's about the livelihoods of majority Zambians women and their children. Land belongs to men, they have the power, but women lack the power to own and combined with discriminatory rules and harmful social and gender norms, at the risk of experiencing gender-based violence heightened. They are denied inheritance rights, evicted from their land, threatened, or have land forcibly taken away. They stay in abusive relationships to have access to land and often experience sexual violence that is also used as a means of control over the land resource. Am standing up for women!"

a6176.speaker: Chief Sunny Onuesoke, environmentalist and managing partner of Das Energy Services Ltd, former governorship aspirant in Delta State
a6176.name: Chief Sunny Onuesoke
a6176.title: environmentalist and managing partner of Das Energy Services Ltd, former governorship aspirant in Delta State
a6176.speech: Urged the Federal Government to cease from undermining local experts, saying local engineers and other experts have the capacity to do jobs hitherto given to expatriates ; said it was baffling that the nation's refineries remained dormant despite decades of promises and billions of naira reportedly spent on Turn Around Maintenance (TAM), regretting that one such national asset is the Warri Refinery ; regretted the continued outsourcing of refinery rehabilitation to foreign companies, explaining that it is not only a wasteful practice but also a vote of no confidence in Nigerian engineers and companies ; "Warri Refinery can be revived by competent engineering companies right here in Warri. I say this not as a sentiment but as a fact rooted in decades of experience" ; "Warri is home to some of the most seasoned engineers, technicians and oil servicing firms in the entire West African region." ; "These professionals have served with distinction in multinationals like Shell, Chevron and Nigerian Petroleum Development Company (NPDC). They are familiar with the terrain, the technology, and more importantly, the culture of the refinery itself." ; "Why then do we constantly overlook these homegrown professionals in favour of foreign companies who neither understand our local context nor offer long-term value beyond expensive consultancy fees?" ; "Let's be clear; this isn't just about national pride. It's about economic sense, local content development, and national security."

a6176.speaker: Chief Sunny Onuesoke, managing partner of Das Energy Services Ltd
a6176.name: Chief Sunny Onuesoke
a6176.title: managing partner of Das Energy Services Ltd
a6176.speech: Called on the Federal Government to save the nation huge foreign exchange by engaging Nigerian engineers to fix the facility, noting that the FG would save the country millions in foreign exchange, empower the local economy, create jobs for unemployed youths and build technical self-reliance; said the Federal Government must break this cycle of dependency and stop the systemic sabotage of local talent: "If a local firm can build modular refineries in Nigeria with private capital and no foreign aid, why should the same government claim that only foreign firms can fix existing state-owned refineries?" ; "We cannot continue this pattern of colonial industrial thinking - where every technical problem must have a foreign solution. It is time to trust Nigerian engineers, particularly those in Warri and the Niger Delta region who have devoted their lives to the oil and gas sector." ; "I call on the Senate, the Federal Ministry of Petroleum, and the NNPC Ltd to urgently reassess their approach. Enough of international contracts that never yield results. Let us put faith in Nigerian hands to solve Nigerian problems." ; "We can fix the Warri Refinery and we can do it with Warri-based engineers."

a6179.speaker: Ethiopian government
a6179.name: Ethiopian government
a6179.speech: Announced it has completed its military offensive after taking the town of Mekele from the so-called criminal group of the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF); announced that the TPLF group had attacked the North National Defense ; said on Tuesday that 44 truckloads of food aid had been delivered to Shire, the main town near the refugee camps.

a6179.speaker: Sekoture Getachew, veteran TPLF politician
a6179.name: Sekoture Getachew
a6179.title: veteran TPLF politician
a6179.speech: Publicly justified the November 4th military attack against the Northern Command of the Ethiopian National Defense Force (ENDF) as an anticipatory self-defense.

a6179.speaker: Redwan Hussein, spokesperson of the state of emergency / Ethiopian government spokesman
a6179.name: Redwan Hussein
a6179.title: spokesperson of the state of emergency / Ethiopian government spokesman
a6179.speech: Told reporters that Ethiopia will invite others for assistance only if it feels that it failed to investigate: "Ethiopia is led by a government which knows how to govern a nation. Ethiopia doesn't need a baby sitter."

a6179.speaker: Redwan Hussein, Ethiopian government spokesman
a6179.name: Redwan Hussein
a6179.title: Ethiopian government spokesman
a6179.speech: Confirmed that Ethiopia's security forces shot to the air and detained United Nations staffers as they tried to reach parts of the embattled Tigray region that they were not supposed to go: "They broke two checkpoints to drive hastily to areas where they were not supposed to go, that they were told not to go." ; "They were told in some areas they were not supposed to move. And when they were left alone they broke two checkpoints, and when they were about to break the third one, soliders shot to the air and detained them. Now, of course they are free."

a6179.speaker: Redwan Hussein, Ethiopian government spokesman
a6179.name: Redwan Hussein
a6179.title: Ethiopian government spokesman
a6179.speech: On humanitarian access: "No entity, multilateral or unilateral, is supposed to supplant the government. We, the government, would call the shots." ; "Humanitarian assistance must be escorted by defense forces." ; "The government will give allowance on where to go and where not to go. There are some forces who have not surrendered. They may not have some regular leadership and command and supply of resources but they can still keep on shooting until they run out of their arms. Thus, we are saying our humanitarian assistance has to be escorted with the military."

a6179.speaker: Redwan Hussein, Ethiopian government spokesman
a6179.name: Redwan Hussein
a6179.title: Ethiopian government spokesman
a6179.speech: On casualties from the operation: "Just because we completed the operation in three weeks it doesn't mean we are in a picnic it was a very tough assignment it was completed successfully because the government was very much conscious about its people. Any life that dies during the operation is a lose to Ethiopia, but we are not hiding anybody killed by the government defense but because there was none there is no one to be accountable other than Ethiopians. It doesn't matter if they were killed by government force or TIgray forces all are Ethiopians, we are not fighting with a foreign enemy it was a family feud."

a6179.speaker: United Nations
a6179.name: United Nations
a6179.speech: Has openly sought unfettered and neutral access according to international principles; announced a deal with the Ethiopian government, saying it was signed on November 29, a deal that allows aid only in areas under Ethiopian government control.

a6179.speaker: Mitiku Kassa, Commissioner of the National Risk and Disaster Management
a6179.name: Mitiku Kassa
a6179.title: Commissioner of the National Risk and Disaster Management
a6179.speech: Said the commission is working to address humanitarian assistance to 1.8 million people in the region; however, with the fear of the number increasing, the commission is working to do a rapid assessment to capture additional numbers of beneficiaries, since between 22-30 percent of the urban population may need relief assistance for a short period of time.

a6223.speaker: Abiy Ahmed, Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a6223.name: Abiy Ahmed
a6223.title: Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a6223.speech: Writes that when he took office in April 2018 he had only one driving mission - to put his country and people on a path to lasting peace and prosperity - and that he vowed "that I would never resort to force as a way of resolving internal political differences", declaring that "the only enemy I would mobilize my people and resources to wage war against was poverty."

a6223.speaker: Abiy Ahmed, Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a6223.name: Abiy Ahmed
a6223.title: Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a6223.speech: States that the TPLF leadership launched a covert and overt campaign to undermine his administration, organizing "a clandestine nationwide campaign of criminality and violence: sponsoring, financing, and training disaffected individuals to instigate communal clashes and attacks on members of ethnic minorities", leaving more than two million people internally displaced and thousands dead; and that he was "fully aware that the TPLF leadership orchestrated the mayhem, bordering on party-sponsored terrorism, diverting budgetary resources allocated by the Federal Government to pay for their criminal enterprise", yet repeatedly refused to use force, invited the TPLF to dialogue and sent senior religious and community leaders to Mekelle, who were rebuffed.

a6223.speaker: Abiy Ahmed, Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a6223.name: Abiy Ahmed
a6223.title: Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a6223.speech: Says that on the night of 03 November 2020 the TPLF leadership attacked the Northern Command of the ENDF, using "traitors recruited from within the army along ethnic lines", massacring unarmed soldiers "in their pyjamas in the dead of night" and seizing the Northern Command's entire military arsenal, leaving him "with a decision only of how, not whether, to fight to defend the integrity of my country and restore the constitutional order"; he attributes three objectives to the attack - weakening the ENDF, dividing it along ethnic lines, and positioning the TPLF to replace the federal government by force.

a6223.speaker: Abiy Ahmed, Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a6223.name: Abiy Ahmed
a6223.title: Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a6223.speech: Writes that the army "has completed its mission according to plan and captured the regional capital of Mekelle without the large-scale civilian casualties and war crimes that so many in the international community confidently predicted", that he is not celebrating, that "the heavy cost we incurred as a nation was necessary", that the next task is healing and ensuring citizens in affected areas, including those who crossed into Sudan, have "unfettered access to humanitarian assistance" and that transport and communication links be restored, and that the government is determined to ensure the elections scheduled for mid-2021 are "fair, free, and inclusive".

a6223.speaker: TPLF leadership (on public television)
a6223.name: TPLF leadership (on public television)
a6223.speech: Described their 03 November attack on the Northern Command as a "lightening pre-emptive attack", and afterwards celebrated and gloated in public about their prowess and invincibility in war and how they had transformed themselves overnight into the largest fighting force in the Horn of Africa.

a6231.speaker: National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a6231.name: National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a6231.speech: Has revealed that Nigeria records approximately 22,000 new HIV infections and 15,000 AIDS-related deaths among children each year.

a6231.speaker: Dr Temitope Ilori, Director General of the National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a6231.name: Dr Temitope Ilori
a6231.title: Director General of the National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
