a6231.speech: Disclosed this on Monday during the 2024 World AIDS Day Press Conference; citing the UNAIDS 2023 report, disclosed that about 160,000 Nigerian children aged 0-14 are living with HIV; noted that the country struggles with preventing mother-to-child transmission (PMTCT) of HIV, with coverage rates still below 33%, far from the 95% global target ; "Despite progress, our PMTCT and pediatric HIV coverage remain inadequate. In 2021, we adopted the Global Alliance Action Plan to End AIDS in Children, but implementation gaps persist. To address this, the Honourable Minister of State for Health has established a national acceleration committee to oversee progress" ; also said Nigeria's HIV prevalence among the general population aged 15-64 stands at 1.4%, with an estimated 2 million people living with HIV.

a6231.speaker: UNAIDS 2023 report
a6231.name: UNAIDS 2023 report
a6231.speech: Cited as the source that about 160,000 Nigerian children aged 0-14 are living with HIV.

a6231.speaker: Funmi Adesanya, Nigeria Country Coordinator of the US-funded President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR)
a6231.name: Funmi Adesanya
a6231.title: Nigeria Country Coordinator of the US-funded President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR)
a6231.speech: Emphasised the importance of sustaining the gains made over the past two decades in providing treatment and reducing new infections; urged stakeholders to address social issues like stigma, discrimination, and structural inequalities that hinder access to care, particularly for marginalized groups.

a6231.speaker: Dr. Patrick Dakum, Chief Executive Officer of the Institute of Human Virology Nigeria (IHVN), represented by Dr Olayemi Olupitan
a6231.name: Dr. Patrick Dakum
a6231.title: Chief Executive Officer of the Institute of Human Virology Nigeria (IHVN), represented by Dr Olayemi Olupitan
a6231.speech: Called for renewed commitment, investment, and innovation.

a6231.speaker: Dr Leo Zekeng, UNAIDS Country Director
a6231.name: Dr Leo Zekeng
a6231.title: UNAIDS Country Director
a6231.speech: Emphasized the need for a sustainable approach, renewed political commitment, and increased domestic funding to identify and place more individuals on treatment.

a6333.speaker: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) (source: MSF statement)
a6333.name: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) (source: MSF statement)
a6333.speech: In 2024, over 7200 children under five years old and pregnant and breastfeeding women from Nyala and surrounding areas were admitted into MSF outpatient feeding programs with severe malnutrition.

a6333.speaker: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) (source: MSF statement)
a6333.name: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) (source: MSF statement)
a6333.speech: Says the scarcity of humanitarian activities run by UN agencies and the lack of a humanitarian response commensurate with the needs imposes challenges on efforts to address the food situation and the overall crisis in South Darfur and across Sudan, resulting in continued gaps in life-saving services, especially the treatment of malnutrition.

a6333.speaker: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) (source: MSF statement)
a6333.name: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) (source: MSF statement)
a6333.speech: “MSF remains committed to addressing the urgent nutritional needs of populations affected by the conflict in South Darfur. The scale of the crisis far exceeds the capacities of the limited numbers of organizations responding to the malnutrition crisis.” ; Says supplies for the treatment of malnutrition, and for food distribution programmes, have to be pre-positioned now before communities are cut off; local responders need funding and support to continue and expand food distribution programmes for their communities; urgent action is needed to scale up humanitarian assistance, and without a concerted effort the crisis will only deepen.

a6333.speaker: Hunter McGovern, MSF's Targeted Food Distribution Project Coordinator in South Darfur
a6333.name: Hunter McGovern
a6333.title: MSF's Targeted Food Distribution Project Coordinator in South Darfur
a6333.speech: “In order to reduce instances where the child's therapeutic food is divided amongst the hungry relatives, we provide a family ration for a duration of two months. This allows the child to receive the full course of their nutrition therapy while increasing the nutritional situation of the whole family. Even with this activity in progress, the needs remain overwhelming.” ; “During our distributions, we found that the average family size is much larger than what we had initially planned for—sometimes as many as ten people per household. This underscores just how critical the food shortage is and how much more assistance is required to meet the real needs of the population.”

a6338.speaker: Fiona Ritchie, British High Commissioner to Malawi, and Professor Bonang Mohale, business leader
a6338.name: Fiona Ritchie
a6338.title: British High Commissioner to Malawi, and Professor Bonang Mohale, business leader
a6338.speech: Have emphasised the critical role of the private sector in driving Malawi's economic transformation. They say the era of abundant development aid is coming to an end and now is time for the private sector to take over.

a6338.speaker: Fiona Ritchie, British High Commissioner to Malawi
a6338.name: Fiona Ritchie
a6338.title: British High Commissioner to Malawi
a6338.speech: Speaking at the Lakeshore Business Leaders' Summit organised by the Malawi Confederation of Chambers of Commerce and Industry (MCCCI) in Mangochi on Friday, Richie called for a shift from an economy built on consumption and government procurement to one based on production, exports, innovation, and private capital. She noted that development aid to Malawi is declining, reflecting a global shift in priorities with a growing expectation that countries must chart their own paths to prosperity. ; “Across the world, it is the private sector that drives growth. It is the private sector that develops solutions, that brings ideas to scale, that powers the engines of industry, agriculture, commerce, and services. Malawi's economy will need to be less dependent on donor funding, and more empowered by private investment. Less focused on managing poverty—and more focused on creating wealth. And trade will be more important than aid.” ; She highlighted mining and energy as two sectors with tremendous potential to drive Malawi's economic transformation.

a6338.speaker: World Bank estimates
a6338.name: World Bank estimates
a6338.speech: World Bank estimates that seven well-developed mining projects could generate exports of at least $30 billion over the next 15 years.

a6338.speaker: Professor Bonang Mohale, business leader
a6338.name: Professor Bonang Mohale
a6338.title: business leader
a6338.speech: In his keynote address titled ‘Unlocking Private Sector-Led Growth: Strategies to Economic Transformation', Mohale emphasised that Africa faces not just another opportunity, but its final chance for economic transformation. ; “This race is not Africa's second chance. It is Africa's last chance. Leadership choices have perpetuated economic challenges across the continent. We need a different kind of business. Not just consciences and taxes, business. But business that fundamentally gets it. That it needs to continue to do well by being good.”

a6358.speaker: Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) FY24 Country Scorecards
a6358.name: Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) FY24 Country Scorecards
a6358.speech: According to the MCC country scorecards for the fiscal year 2024 (FY24 Country Scorecards), released on Tuesday (November 7), with data from independent organisations essentially referring to the year 2022, Mozambique does maintain a “red” negative assessment in the areas of Fiscal Policy (42% assessment), Political Rights (score of 14 out of a positive minimum of 17), Land Rights and Access (41% rating), Immunisation Rates (35%) and Child Health (41%), as in the previous report. ; However, Mozambique secured a “green” positive rating in the areas of Rule of Law (52% rating), Girls Primary Education Completion Rates (56%) and Education Expenditures (97%). ; Mozambique also improved in the Freedom of Information scorecard, in this case with data from 2023, passing a positive assessment, with a record of 70%, up from 48% in the 2023 fiscal year report.

a6358.speaker: Alice Albright, president of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a6358.name: Alice Albright
a6358.title: president of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a6358.speech: stated at the time that the US$500 million donation for connectivity and coastal resilience projects represents a “marking moment” in relations with Mozambique. “We will help, we estimate, 15 million Mozambicans over the next 20 years in various aspects of daily life. We will help to improve fisheries, transport, agriculture and youth and women’s prospects,” Albright said after signing Mozambique’s second financing compact with Max Tonela, Mozambique’s Minister of Economy and Finance.

a6358.speaker: Alice Albright, president of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a6358.name: Alice Albright
a6358.title: president of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a6358.speech: “The MCC is very selective with the countries it works with. We work with countries that are democracies, that seek to invest in people and improve their economies, and that is why launching this Compact is a remarkable moment in relations between the two countries,” Allbright further explained in statements to journalists after the signing of the agreement. ; “The United States is incredibly proud of the relationship it has with Mozambique and my agency, which is part of the US government, and feels deeply honoured to be able to sign our second agreement with Mozambique. […] We started our first agreement in 2004 and will work on the second agreement in several areas, to help the country with some of the climate impacts [it faces],” the MCC president added.

a6448.speaker: Bola Tinubu, President of Nigeria
a6448.name: Bola Tinubu
a6448.title: President of Nigeria
a6448.speech: Announced the appointment of Mr. Ayo Sotinrin as the new Managing Director of the Bank of Agriculture ; “Mr Sotinrin's proven ability to mobilise capital, innovate in agribusiness, and collaborate across sectors will be instrumental in repositioning the Bank of Agriculture as a catalyst for food security, sovereignty and rural prosperity”, President Tinubu emphasised.

a6448.speaker: Bayo Onanuga, Tinubu's media aide (statement)
a6448.name: Bayo Onanuga
a6448.title: Tinubu's media aide (statement)
a6448.speech: Said the appointment takes immediate effect ; also noted that Mr. Sotinrin brings a diverse and extensive background in the private and public sectors to his new role.

a6456.speaker: Residents and authorities in the enclave (Gaza)
a6456.name: Residents and authorities in the enclave (Gaza)
a6456.speech: Said Israel airstrikes killed at least 70 people in Gaza overnight on Thursday.

a6456.speaker: An Israeli official (anonymous)
a6456.name: An Israeli official (anonymous)
a6456.speech: Said Israel's acceptance of the deal will not be official until it is approved by the country's security cabinet and government, and that a vote was slated for Thursday.

a6456.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli Prime Minister
a6456.name: Benjamin Netanyahu
a6456.title: Israeli Prime Minister
a6456.speech: Accused Hamas of making last-minute demands and going back on agreements.

a6456.speaker: Statement from Netanyahu's office
a6456.name: Statement from Netanyahu's office
a6456.speech: “The Israeli cabinet will not convene until the mediators notify Israel that Hamas has accepted all elements of the agreement.”

a6456.speaker: Izzat el-Reshiq, senior Hamas official
a6456.name: Izzat el-Reshiq
a6456.title: senior Hamas official
a6456.speech: Said on Thursday that Hamas is committed to the ceasefire agreement announced by mediators on Wednesday.

a6456.speaker: Bezalel Smotrich, Israeli Finance Minister
a6456.name: Bezalel Smotrich
a6456.title: Israeli Finance Minister
a6456.speech: Said his party would only stay in the government if Israel resumes the war full force until Hamas is defeated.

a6456.speaker: Itamar Ben-Gvir, Israeli far-right police minister
a6456.name: Itamar Ben-Gvir
a6456.title: Israeli far-right police minister
a6456.speech: Has also threatened to quit the government if the ceasefire is approved.

a6456.speaker: Mahmoud Abu Wardeh, Gazan man
a6456.name: Mahmoud Abu Wardeh
a6456.title: Gazan man
a6456.speech: “We lose homes every hour. We demand for this joy not to go away, the joy that was drawn on our faces – don't waste it by delaying the implementation of the truce until Sunday.”

a6456.speaker: The civil emergency service and residents
a6456.name: The civil emergency service and residents
a6456.speech: Said that while people celebrated the pact in Gaza and Israel, Israel's military conducted more attacks.

a6456.speaker: Mahmoud Basal, spokesperson for the Palestinian Civil Emergency Service
a6456.name: Mahmoud Basal
a6456.title: spokesperson for the Palestinian Civil Emergency Service
a6456.speech: Said in a statement that 71 Palestinians had been killed and at least 200 others wounded.

a6456.speaker: Israeli military spokesperson
a6456.name: Israeli military spokesperson
a6456.speech: Said the Israeli military is looking into the reports.

a6456.speaker: Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, Qatari Prime Minister
a6456.name: Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani
a6456.title: Qatari Prime Minister
a6456.speech: Said at a news conference in Doha that negotiators are working with Israel and Hamas on steps to implement the agreement.

a6456.speaker: Joe Biden, U.S. President
a6456.name: Joe Biden
a6456.title: U.S. President
a6456.speech: “This deal will halt the fighting in Gaza, surge much-needed humanitarian assistance to Palestinian civilians, and reunite the hostages with their families after more than 15 months in captivity.”

a6456.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect
a6456.name: Donald Trump
a6456.title: US President-elect
a6456.speech: Claimed credit for the breakthrough in Gaza.

a6456.speaker: Successive surveys (of Israeli public opinion)
a6456.name: Successive surveys (of Israeli public opinion)
a6456.speech: Have shown broad support among the public for a deal that would see the hostages released, even at what is seen as a heavy price.

a6456.speaker: Chava Treitel, Jerusalem resident
a6456.name: Chava Treitel
a6456.title: Jerusalem resident
a6456.speech: “This has to be the only choice that we take in order to continue surviving as a state and as a nation, knowing that we will do anything to save each other.”

a6456.speaker: Gaza authorities
a6456.name: Gaza authorities
a6456.speech: According to Gaza authorities, the fighting has razed much of heavily urbanised Gaza, killed over 46,000 people, and displaced most of the enclave's pre-war population of 2.3 million.

a6456.speaker: The U.N. and the International Committee of the Red Cross
a6456.name: The U.N. and the International Committee of the Red Cross
a6456.speech: Said they were preparing to scale up their aid operations.

a6456.speaker: Israeli tallies
a6456.name: Israeli tallies
a6456.speech: According to Israeli tallies, Hamas-led gunmen burst into Israeli border-area communities on Oct. 7, 2023, killing 1,200 soldiers and civilians and abducting over 250 hostages.

a7210.speaker: African Development Bank (AfDB)
a7210.name: African Development Bank (AfDB)
a7210.speech: Says that the continent loses about $1.6bn every day to illicit financial flows and profit shifting on the part of multinationals operating in Africa.

a7210.speaker: Kevin Urama, Chief Economist of the AfDB
a7210.name: Kevin Urama
a7210.title: Chief Economist of the AfDB
a7210.speech: Told the Nigerian Punch newspaper that Africa was losing more than it was getting back via Foreign Direct Investment and that the focus of stakeholders should be on blocking the outflow rather than chasing inflows ; “There are so many things that happen on the continent that actually make corruption a big issue. And some estimations show that Africa loses about 248 billion US dollars every year due to corruption. If you add illicit financial flows of over $90bn and add profit shifting; corporates operating in Africa but then maybe have headquarters somewhere else and they find clever accounting ways of legally not paying taxes. In Africa, we are losing about $275bn. When you sum all these up, these are things you can trace through banks, then you find that Africa is losing about $587bn every year. That’s about $1.61bn every day. Yet we spend all our time chasing FDI, foreign direct investment, official development assistance, portfolio flows and remittances. All these together during the year we did this study for 2022 was about $174.5bn. That’s less than three times, I mean what we are losing is three times more than what we are getting from the global market. So how do we engage with the global market? Are we not focusing on the wrong priorities? Because if you ask me if I’m losing almost $600bn, I will focus on how not to lose it instead of going to get more. Tackling it, is what we are doing,” he said.

a7210.speaker: Kevin Urama, Chief Economist of the AfDB
a7210.name: Kevin Urama
a7210.title: Chief Economist of the AfDB
a7210.speech: Highlighting some of the ways to shut the door on the outflow, Urama said, “It all comes down to the quality of institutions, the accountability systems for institutions, the capacity of individuals in government, in public service to first understand the implications of decisions they make but also to have the tools, the regulations, the policies and principles and technologies to be able to track it down and stem it. And that is why in the African Development Bank, we not only are developing these issues on debt but we’ve also now developed what we call a Public Service Delivery Index for Africa which measures the quantum of public services delivered in all key sectors of development but also the perceptions of the citizens on how that public service is. You may say you have provided electricity to me because you put a pole and wires passed behind my house, but maybe I have not been able to connect.”

a7210.speaker: Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit
a7210.name: Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit
a7210.speech: Said in October that FAFT had approved the fourth progress report of the country at its last plenary meeting.

a7336.speaker: International Labour Organisation (ILO)
a7336.name: International Labour Organisation (ILO)
a7336.speech: Said that in implementing the National Development Vision 2050 it is important that Tanzania prioritise decent work, because that is the foundation of peace and social stability in society.

a7336.speaker: Caroline Mugalla, ILO Director for the East Africa Region
a7336.name: Caroline Mugalla
a7336.title: ILO Director for the East Africa Region
a7336.speech: "Decent work is the foundation of peace, social stability and inclusive development. Without ensuring dignity, protection and opportunity for every worker, whether in the formal or the informal sector, we cannot achieve true development." ; Said Tanzania's Vision 2050 is not merely an economic plan but a social contract aimed at ensuring inclusive growth, and that justice and opportunity are expanded to all citizens. ; "Vision 2050 is a call to action. We must stand with courage and creativity to ensure that every Tanzanian can look at their tomorrow with dignity, security and hope." ; Stressed that if Tanzania wants to achieve its 2050 goals it will have to prioritise decent work, gender inclusion, safety at work and reducing unemployment, especially among young people.

a7336.speaker: Caroline Mugalla, ILO Director for the East Africa Region
a7336.name: Caroline Mugalla
a7336.title: ILO Director for the East Africa Region
a7336.speech: Said trade unions have a duty to ensure that the voices of all groups of workers are heard and their needs met: "Unions must continue to defend rights, and must also be innovative in helping workers to cope with the challenges of digitalisation, climate change and globalisation."

a7336.speaker: Caroline Mugalla, ILO Director for the East Africa Region
a7336.name: Caroline Mugalla
a7336.title: ILO Director for the East Africa Region
a7336.speech: Called on employers to lead by combining business competitiveness with social responsibility, investing in skills training for young people, improving safe working environments and supporting jobs that protect the environment while increasing productivity.

a7336.speaker: Caroline Mugalla, ILO Director for the East Africa Region
a7336.name: Caroline Mugalla
a7336.title: ILO Director for the East Africa Region
a7336.speech: Said government institutions have a duty to ensure an environment that allows decent work to exist, while the courts and the Commission for Mediation and Arbitration (CMA) should deliver justice in a timely manner so that citizens trust the labour justice system; called on the Occupational Safety and Health Authority (OSHA) to strengthen safety at work, because no one should risk their life in order to earn an income, and called on social security institutions to widen their scope to reach the informal sector.

a7336.speaker: Caroline Mugalla, ILO Director for the East Africa Region
a7336.name: Caroline Mugalla
a7336.title: ILO Director for the East Africa Region
a7336.speech: "The informal sector is the main source of income for most Tanzanians, but its workers remain without protection. Formalisation is not a matter of complying with the law alone; it is a matter of dignity, equality and national development."

a7336.speaker: Caroline Mugalla, ILO Director for the East Africa Region
a7336.name: Caroline Mugalla
a7336.title: ILO Director for the East Africa Region
a7336.speech: Stressed that young people should be given priority because they are the largest group of Tanzanians and the foundation of tomorrow's nation: "If they are given skills, opportunities and support in innovation, young people cannot merely carry the nation, but push it forward."

a7336.speaker: Caroline Mugalla, ILO Director for the East Africa Region
a7336.name: Caroline Mugalla
a7336.title: ILO Director for the East Africa Region
a7336.speech: Said regarding people with disabilities that they should be seen as a resource and not a social burden, calling on the government, employers and society to remove barriers, prepare friendly environments and change attitudes in order to achieve genuine inclusion.

a7336.speaker: Caroline Mugalla, ILO Director for the East Africa Region
a7336.name: Caroline Mugalla
a7336.title: ILO Director for the East Africa Region
a7336.speech: Said that since its founding the ILO has been built on cooperation between government, employers and workers, and that this philosophy is the catalyst for achieving long-term development; appealed to stakeholders to cooperate, listen to one another and seek joint solutions to the challenges facing the employment sector, promising that the ILO will continue to work with Tanzania to strengthen institutions, expand social protection and develop inclusive labour markets.

a7462.speaker: Dr Mu'azu Babangida Aliyu, Chairman of the Sir Ahmadu Bello Memorial Foundation
a7462.name: Dr Mu'azu Babangida Aliyu
a7462.title: Chairman of the Sir Ahmadu Bello Memorial Foundation
a7462.speech: Stated that the Northern part of Nigeria is at war against itself and gradually disintegrating, and that the region needs urgent attention to salvage it from total collapse: "If you look around very well, there are some who are busy running down the North. It is not only USAID that is our problem; there are those who are instigating Hausa fighting Fulani and other things. These are the things we must urgently take care of before we are consumed." ; "These segments of the people are using every available divisive measure to further aggravate our poverty situation and perpetrate all forms of evils among our people." ; "We must be very careful, do away with every materialistic tendency, and unite our people, make our region better and stronger."

a7462.speaker: Dr Mu'azu Babangida Aliyu, Chairman of the Sir Ahmadu Bello Memorial Foundation
a7462.name: Dr Mu'azu Babangida Aliyu
a7462.title: Chairman of the Sir Ahmadu Bello Memorial Foundation
a7462.speech: Eulogised the lives and times of Nigeria's founding fathers, including the late Ahmadu Bello, Abubakar Tafawa Balewa, and a host of others, for bequeathing a legacy of unity on the north while they ruled, stressing that such must not be allowed to die.

a7462.speaker: Bala Mohammed Abdulkadir, Governor of Bauchi State
a7462.name: Bala Mohammed Abdulkadir
a7462.title: Governor of Bauchi State
a7462.speech: In his response, stressed the importance of unity and regional integration in Nigeria, calling on leaders to work together to address the country's challenges, particularly in the areas of poverty, security and education; emphasised the importance of learning from the past, saying that the legacy of Nigeria's past leaders, such as Ahmadu Bello, should be built upon to promote unity and development; said there is the need for leaders to be guided by principles and to prioritize the interests of the people, adding that the country's diversity should be celebrated: "Unity is essential for progress, the trust deficit between the government and the people is a significant obstacle to development, and efforts should be made to bridge this gap."

a7509.speaker: The organisers of the "Cotonou nuits blues" festival (press conference)
a7509.name: The organisers of the "Cotonou nuits blues" festival (press conference)
a7509.speech: made it known yesterday, at a press conference given at the diaspora media library of the Place des Martyrs in Cotonou, that the objective of the "Cotonou nuits blues" festival is to promote Beninese music, notably the blues, and to create a cultural mixing.

a7509.speaker: The organiser (Bonaventure Dossou-Yovo, initiator of the festival)
a7509.name: The organiser (Bonaventure Dossou-Yovo
a7509.title: initiator of the festival)
a7509.speech: According to the organiser, the initiative for this festival was taken because Benin is a country rich in cultures that must be sold and exported; the "blues", which has its origins in Africa, is one of the facets of this richness, and in choosing to devote a festival to it for the first time in Benin, it is a well-deserved return to the roots.

a7509.speaker: The organiser (Bonaventure Dossou-Yovo, initiator of the festival)
a7509.name: The organiser (Bonaventure Dossou-Yovo
a7509.title: initiator of the festival)
a7509.speech: According to the organiser, "Cotonou nuits blues" is an event that is intended to be periodic.
